a1.speaker: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh, Director General of the National Agency for Employment, Training and Professional Insertion (ANEFIP)
a1.name: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh
a1.title: Director General of the National Agency for Employment, Training and Professional Insertion (ANEFIP)
a1.speech: "All job seekers benefit from internships. We place them in a company either through a paid internship — that is, for a maximum of 3 months, during which the intern carries out activities in the company but is not paid — or through another type called a 'paid internship,' where most beneficiaries generally hold degrees and therefore have high added value. So these people are placed in companies for 5 years, where they are paid up to 50,000 FD per month."

a1.speaker: Neima Hassan Ismaël, Director of Sectoral Monitoring and Foresight, General Directorate of Technical Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1.name: Neima Hassan Ismaël
a1.title: Director of Sectoral Monitoring and Foresight, General Directorate of Technical Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a1.speech: Described her structure as well as the challenges and opportunities she sees in supporting the placement of young people in internships.

a1.speaker: Idil Aden Robleh, Director of the Training Center, Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a1.name: Idil Aden Robleh
a1.title: Director of the Training Center, Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a1.speech: Described her structure as well as the challenges and opportunities she sees in supporting the placement of young people in internships.

a1.speaker: Bogoreh Ali Meidal, 2nd Vice President of the Association of Djiboutian Freight Forwarders
a1.name: Bogoreh Ali Meidal
a1.title: 2nd Vice President of the Association of Djiboutian Freight Forwarders
a1.speech: Emphasized the benefits that internships bring to companies ; "Personally, I work in the logistics profession; when interns are sent to me, the first thing I look for is whether or not they are passionate about this profession." ; "Some interns have all the qualities we are looking for; in that case we talk with them and encourage them not to leave." ; "The intern allows us to expand the scope of our work. That is to say, there are tasks that we don't have time to do in the logistics profession. We are too busy with operations to carry out and so we forget certain tasks like filing, file tracking, accounts, container returns, etc. And these things, we pass on to the interns. So we use them. It's win-win, at first. That's why as soon as we have an intern, I sit down with him and make clear to him that we work in a win-win process. He certainly needs me and I need him to carry out certain tasks of great importance to us. There is also another advantage that allows us to identify and appreciate someone. During my career, I have had many interns and there are some whose work I really appreciated. Because they had all the qualities we are looking for. In that case we talk with them and encourage them not to leave the company and not to go elsewhere."

a87.speaker: US Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a87.name: US Embassy in South Sudan (press statement)
a87.speech: Said it is working with partners, including UNICEF, IOM, MSF and WHO, to deliver emergency water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, provide life-saving medical care, support vaccination campaigns, provide treatment kits and diagnostic tests, and raise public awareness to curb the spread of cholera. Said: "On December 29, we delivered more than two million Aquatab water purification tablets as part of the humanitarian response to South Sudan's ongoing cholera outbreak," providing safe drinking water to communities most affected by the outbreak. Said the United States has committed $200,000 to the World Health Organization to support cholera response activities in South Sudan, which will enhance public awareness campaigns, strengthen WASH interventions, and equip health officials with resources to treat cases effectively. Said: "The United States stands with the people of South Sudan during this challenging time. This assistance will save lives and help prevent the spread of cholera in vulnerable communities. At the same time, we renew our call on South Sudan's transitional government to start using public revenue to address its people's health needs, provide other basic services, and to pay public sector salaries for health workers, other civil servants, and security personnel."

a221.speaker: Sharma'arke Yaasiin Beeldaaje, former Director of the Puntland Ministry of Fisheries
a221.name: Sharma'arke Yaasiin Beeldaaje
a221.title: former Director of the Puntland Ministry of Fisheries
a221.speech: Denied that he embezzled money from the ministry, saying there is no one who can produce proof of the accusation made against him, and that there was no money he took and that the claim was fabricated. "There is no place where I took money and no one who can prove it; it is a fabrication and completely baseless. Minister Xagaa has always insulted people and he will not get away with this one, proof of it is required," said Sharma'arke Beeldaaje Yaasiin.

a221.speaker: Sharma'arke Yaasiin Beeldaaje, former Director of the Puntland Ministry of Fisheries
a221.name: Sharma'arke Yaasiin Beeldaaje
a221.title: former Director of the Puntland Ministry of Fisheries
a221.speech: Accused Minister Xagaa of having secret links with the terrorist group Daesh (ISIS), although he did not present any evidence showing the truth of his statement, other than mere accusation.

a221.speaker: Cabdirisaaq Cabdullaahi Xagaa, Puntland Minister of Fisheries
a221.name: Cabdirisaaq Cabdullaahi Xagaa
a221.title: Puntland Minister of Fisheries
a221.speech: The accusation that the former director had embezzled money from the ministry came from him.

a334.speaker: Solomon Muchie, DW correspondent covering the African Union in Addis Ababa
a334.name: Solomon Muchie
a334.title: DW correspondent covering the African Union in Addis Ababa
a334.speech: “The competition was between a politician and a diplomat, and it was very tough. It went to the seventh round of voting.”

a334.speaker: Solomon Muchie, DW correspondent covering the African Union in Addis Ababa
a334.name: Solomon Muchie
a334.title: DW correspondent covering the African Union in Addis Ababa
a334.speech: “Djibouti is a small but very critical state in this region,” pointing out that the United States, China, France, Italy and Japan all have military bases in Djibouti ; “This is also the corridor for Asia, Europe and Africa trade routes.”

a334.speaker: Macharia Munene, Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.name: Macharia Munene
a334.title: Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.speech: “If they are united in thought, they might be able to develop a common agenda, but it’s a tall order.”

a334.speaker: Macharia Munene, Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.name: Macharia Munene
a334.title: Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.speech: Said it was “no surprise” that Youssouf defeated veteran Kenyan politician Raila Odinga, and that the positions Kenya has taken recently are contrary to AU interests. “The fact that Kenya is hosting the rebel side of the Sudanese civil war, of course, will make some other countries very unhappy.”

a334.speaker: Macharia Munene, Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.name: Macharia Munene
a334.title: Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.speech: Told DW the AU’s ineffectiveness lies not just in weak funding: “It first needs to resolve internal divisions, some of them ideological, others simply personal disputes” ; said that without solving these problems first, it is hard to see the AU effectively addressing “big problems right now, like Sudan and the DR Congo.”

a334.speaker: Macharia Munene, Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.name: Macharia Munene
a334.title: Kenyan analyst and professor of history and international relations
a334.speech: “The issue of reparations has been around for a long time and it’s a good PR issue. The implementation of it, of course, is a big problem” ; sees challenges in getting European countries, which have seen a surge in far-right popularity, to agree to any form of reparation, and says the United States has also been “cutting, cutting, cutting” aid.

a334.speaker: Dareskedar Taye, Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.name: Dareskedar Taye
a334.title: Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.speech: Told DW it was good that Youssouf is from the Horn of Africa. “If effort and desire is added in improving Ethiopia’s relationship with Djibouti from its current level, I think this can be good” ; added that although Ethiopia maintains ties with Kenya, “Djibouti is our only way-out country in terms of port access.”

a334.speaker: Dareskedar Taye, Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.name: Dareskedar Taye
a334.title: Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.speech: “It is expected that the aid and support provided to the African Union from Western countries will decrease significantly.”

a334.speaker: Dareskedar Taye, Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.name: Dareskedar Taye
a334.title: Ethiopian analyst at the Institute of Foreign Affairs
a334.speech: “The AU requires institutional reform, because the African Union is not doing much for Africans. For example, the financial capacity is weak. Now, new leaders have come forward; maybe they can improve it.”

a334.speaker: American officials
a334.name: American officials
a334.speech: A string of statements from American officials came, implying that Europe would have to take care of its own security.

a334.speaker: Some observers / others (unnamed commentators)
a334.name: Some observers / others (unnamed commentators)
a334.speech: Some observers have questioned the timing of the AU’s call for reparations, while others have said now is the right time for European countries looking for allies in the wake of the Trump administration’s America First foreign policy to strike deals with former African colonies.

a379.speaker: Mike Rogers, Republican Representative from Alabama and Chairman of the US House Armed Services Committee
a379.name: Mike Rogers
a379.title: Republican Representative from Alabama and Chairman of the US House Armed Services Committee
a379.speech: “We came to meet President Patrice Talon to discuss security and economic cooperation between Benin and the United States of America. It is a bipartisan delegation, therefore composed of members of the parliamentary majority and the parliamentary minority.” ; “We are making this visit to the African continent in order to discuss with our African partners and understand their defence and security needs and what we can do to accompany African countries. We can support Benin on several fronts.”

a379.speaker: Sara Jacobs, Democratic Representative from California, member of the US House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs Committees
a379.name: Sara Jacobs
a379.title: Democratic Representative from California, member of the US House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs Committees
a379.speech: Indicated that the United States has put in place, over the next ten years, a bilateral cooperation strategy to support the coastal regions of Africa, in which Benin is taken into account. “We want to make sure of the work being done at the security level but also in the area of development with USAID. While we are supporting Benin at the security level, we want to ensure that the security needs are substantial as regards the north of the country,” before qualifying that her country is making sure the work is being done for the economic development of the populations in those regions and that those populations understand that their well-being is paramount for everyone.

a379.speaker: Patrice Talon, President of the Republic of Benin
a379.name: Patrice Talon
a379.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a379.speech: Reiterated to his guests Benin's commitment and permanent availability to work together with the United States in achieving defence and security objectives in the African coastal zone; insisted on the importance of bilateral military cooperation, training activities for military personnel, the supply of equipment, military infrastructure and exchanges of experience.

a467.speaker: US State Department, Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for Liberia (published 12 August 2025)
a467.name: US State Department
a467.title: Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for Liberia (published 12 August 2025)
a467.speech: Highlights a troubling pattern of disregard for the rule of law in Liberia, specifically emphasizing the alarming number of detainees who remain incarcerated for extended periods without being brought to trial. According to the report, approximately 60 percent of pretrial detainees, with a significant focus on those facing felony charges, are held for over 180 days—far surpassing the legal limit of two court terms without a hearing; the report underscores that while Liberian law mandates the dismissal of cases that are not prosecuted within this timeframe, such case dismissals are “rarely” enacted.

a467.speaker: US State Department, Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for Liberia
a467.name: US State Department
a467.title: Country Reports on Human Rights Practices for Liberia
a467.speech: Identifies several serious human rights violations occurring in the country during the review period, including credible reports of arbitrary or unlawful killings, instances of torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, arbitrary arrests or detention, restrictions on freedom of expression and media rights exposing journalists to violence and threats, censorship, widespread trafficking in persons, and systematic limitations on workers’ freedom of association.

a467.speaker: Judge of a Monrovia criminal court
a467.name: Judge of a Monrovia criminal court
a467.speech: In November, publicly reprimanded prosecutors from the Ministry of Justice for their inadequate handling of the case involving Ibrahim Kalil Cherif, a Guinean national accused of conspiring to orchestrate a coup, and threatened to hold the Justice Ministry in contempt of court, openly criticizing the government’s handling of the case before it was ultimately closed.

a467.speaker: Liberian government
a467.name: Liberian government
a467.speech: Defended this controversial action – removing Cherif from prison without any court order and handing him over to Guinean authorities at their request – as a necessary measure for national security, disregarding legal protocols.

a540.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a540.name: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a540.speech: Has confirmed that treatment for HIV in Nigeria remains free, in spite of ongoing funding challenges.

a540.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a540.name: Temitope Ilori
a540.title: Director-General of NACA
a540.speech: Highlighted President Bola Tinubu's commitment to ending HIV in the country, noting the allocation of N300 billion to fight the disease and address other health-related issues in spite of financial constraints ; noted that President Bola Tinubu had set aside a budget to ensure that HIV-related services continued uninterrupted and that necessary commodities remained available.

a540.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a540.name: Temitope Ilori
a540.title: Director-General of NACA
a540.speech: Emphasised that the US government was not Nigeria's only partner in the fight against HIV, as several other countries also supported Nigeria's efforts, particularly in the PMTCT programme ; noted the collaborative efforts of the federal and state governments, alongside other stakeholders, to combat HIV ; "The fight against HIV is a collective effort and together, we can change the narrative."

a540.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a540.name: Temitope Ilori
a540.title: Director-General of NACA
a540.speech: Explained that the current focus was to address the challenge of mother-to-child transmission in the country: "We are here to inaugurate the Delta State Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission of HIV and the Paediatric HIV Acceleration Committee. A similar committee has been inaugurated at the national level, and states, as major stakeholders, are replicating it locally." ; said the newly established committee, which included various stakeholders, aimed to ensure that pregnant women had access to antenatal care, and encouraged pregnant women to get tested for HIV during antenatal visits: "If pregnant women test positive, they will receive antiretroviral treatment to reduce the risk of transmitting the virus to their child."

a540.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a540.name: Temitope Ilori
a540.title: Director-General of NACA
a540.speech: Expressed concern that Nigeria had the highest burden of children born with HIV, with the current national infection rate at 1.4 per cent and Delta State's at 1.9 per cent, but stressed that efforts were being made to reduce these numbers.

a540.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of NACA
a540.name: Temitope Ilori
a540.title: Director-General of NACA
a540.speech: Assured that HIV drugs remained completely free and available at primary healthcare centres, secondary facilities, and teaching hospitals, emphasising that both the test and the treatment were provided at no cost to patients, as the federal government had allocated the necessary resources.

a540.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier report)
a540.name: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier report)
a540.speech: Reported that the US government recently halted funding to support the fight against HIV in Nigeria and other countries; although that halt was temporarily reversed, the US under new President Donald Trump also cut funding for many health and development projects in Nigeria and other countries through USAID.

a540.speaker: Joseph Onojaeme, Delta State Commissioner for Health (represented by Philomena Okeowo, permanent secretary of the ministry)
a540.name: Joseph Onojaeme
a540.title: Delta State Commissioner for Health (represented by Philomena Okeowo, permanent secretary of the ministry)
a540.speech: Stated that the timing of the committee's inauguration was crucial, and pledged the state's support to eliminate mother-to-child HIV transmission in Delta.

a540.speaker: Hobson Rudolf, executive secretary of the Delta State Agency for Control of AIDS (DELSACA)
a540.name: Hobson Rudolf
a540.title: executive secretary of the Delta State Agency for Control of AIDS (DELSACA)
a540.speech: Added that the new multi-sectoral committee would work to develop a clear roadmap whose goal was to reduce HIV transmission from mother to child in the state: "As of now, approximately 62,000 people in Delta State are living with HIV, representing 1.9 per cent of the population. HIV drugs are accessible and free at all facilities across the state."

a540.speaker: Faith-based organisations
a540.name: Faith-based organisations
a540.speech: Pledged their commitment to the shared goals.

a540.speaker: UNAIDS 2023 report
a540.name: UNAIDS 2023 report
a540.speech: Indicated that Nigeria continued to struggle with preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission, with about 140,000 children aged 0-14 living with HIV, 22,000 new infections and 15,000 AIDS-related deaths annually: "The coverage for PMTCT and pediatric HIV treatment remains below 33 per cent, falling short of the 95 per cent target set by global initiatives. The Global Alliance Action Plan to End AIDS in Children, launched in 2021, has yet to achieve optimal coverage."

a688.speaker: 21st ordinary session of Mali's National Food Security Council (CNSA), chaired by Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maiga
a688.name: 21st ordinary session of Mali's National Food Security Council (CNSA)
a688.title: chaired by Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maiga
a688.speech: Called on the Food Security Commission to continue the reforms, in particular through the creation of the Food and Nutrition Security Monitoring and Early Warning Agency (AVASAN), which will play a central role in the preventive management of crises.

a790.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a790.name: Donald Trump
a790.title: US President-elect
a790.speech: Has already promised to impose significant tariffs on foreign imports, but his position on the future of AGOA, which is due to be renewed next year, is unclear.

a790.speaker: Ronak Gopaldas, consultant at the Institute for Security Studies (ISS)
a790.name: Ronak Gopaldas
a790.title: consultant at the Institute for Security Studies (ISS)
a790.speech: "Under a Trump administration, with its 'America First' mantra, trade policy would probably be insular and transactional. Given Trump's scepticism towards multilateral frameworks, the survival of AGOA could legitimately be under threat." ; Notes that while "Africa may not be among the priorities" of Trump, "his first administration pushed for trade deals with certain hand-picked African countries, which suggests a preference for bilateral engagement."

a790.speaker: General Michael Langley, head of the US military command for Africa (Africom)
a790.name: General Michael Langley
a790.title: head of the US military command for Africa (Africom)
a790.speech: In September, reported discussions with other African partners in order to "reset and recalibrate" American military assistance on the continent.

a790.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a790.name: Donald Trump
a790.title: US President-elect
a790.speech: Has already criticised the billions of dollars spent by the United States on Ukraine.

a790.speaker: US State Department
a790.name: US State Department
a790.speech: According to the State Department, the United States is an important provider of aid to Africa, with $4 billion (3.7 billion euros) planned for 2024.

a790.speaker: Some South African media
a790.name: Some South African media
a790.speech: Are already wondering whether the American programme of aid for the fight against HIV, called Pepfar, will continue.

a790.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a790.name: Donald Trump
a790.title: US President-elect
a790.speech: Has described climate change as a hoax, and has pledged to roll back the environmental measures taken by his predecessor.

a790.speaker: Mohamed Adow, Kenyan activist and director of the NGO Power Shift Africa (statement)
a790.name: Mohamed Adow
a790.title: Kenyan activist and director of the NGO Power Shift Africa (statement)
a790.speech: "The world has experienced (the first) Trump presidency and the American withdrawal from the Paris agreement. His return (...) is a moment of profound apprehension in global climate diplomacy."

a806.speaker: Joshua Nzengo, resident of Tandala hamlet and service recipient
a806.name: Joshua Nzengo
a806.title: resident of Tandala hamlet and service recipient
a806.speech: Said that previously they faced the challenge of travelling a long distance of about 50 kilometres and spending a lot of money to reach the district headquarters to go to the hospital and collect medicines and counselling: “The fare from here to the district is 10,000 shillings by bus for the round trip; for citizens like us of low means who depend on farming, it is hard to go every week to fetch medicine. ; “Sometimes you stay at home for a whole month without medicine and that causes your health to become weak, so this step of bringing the service closer to us has helped us a great deal.”

a806.speaker: Joseph Kulwa, service recipient
a806.name: Joseph Kulwa
a806.title: service recipient
a806.speech: Said that apart from the high costs of getting to those services, they used to spend nearly a whole day fetching them: “We used to spend the whole day going to town to fetch services and by the time we returned it was already evening, so we could no longer do any productive activities; therefore bringing the service closer makes it easier for us to collect medicine and go on with our daily activities.”

a806.speaker: Said Hamis, nurse in the treatment and care unit for people living with HIV at Uvinza Health Centre
a806.name: Said Hamis
a806.title: nurse in the treatment and care unit for people living with HIV at Uvinza Health Centre
a806.speech: Said the mobile clinic is offered twice a month and that so far they have more than 280 service recipients at the Tandala site ; said the M-koba service began in 2019 and since its establishment it has made it easier for service recipients to arrive on time and collect medicines without fail on every clinic date, a step that has helped improve their health while they continue with their daily responsibilities without obstacles.

a806.speaker: Dr Gabriel Max, Afya Hatua Project Manager for Uvinza district
a806.name: Dr Gabriel Max
a806.title: Afya Hatua Project Manager for Uvinza district
a806.speech: Said that in that council they have 16 centres providing services including treatment and care for people living with HIV, testing, cervical cancer screening, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, prevention and male circumcision ; said citizens live far from the places where services are received and, recognising this, in collaboration with the Government they brought the services closer: “These M-koba services are provided in 36 locations in Uvinza and they are no different from the services offered at the health centre, because the providers are the same, the medicines, the tests and the counselling service; the aim is to reduce the distance and costs for service recipients.”

a813.speaker: Izbath Djaboutouboutou, Director of Self-Referral (Auto-saisine) at the Office of the Ombudsman of the Republic and project focal point
a813.name: Izbath Djaboutouboutou
a813.title: Director of Self-Referral (Auto-saisine) at the Office of the Ombudsman of the Republic and project focal point
a813.speech: Said that the civic engagement and leadership of young people are valuable resources only if they are cultivated and supported; noted that thanks to the various teams deployed in the seven communes of the northern departments, 1,282 young women and men have been trained and are now equipped to contribute actively to the development of their communities and, by extension, to the development of the country; these young people, bearers of hope and ambition, are now better prepared to take part in building the nation with an emphasis on peace and national unity.

a813.speaker: Abigail Slenski, Deputy Country Representative of USAID in Benin
a813.name: Abigail Slenski
a813.title: Deputy Country Representative of USAID in Benin
a813.speech: Observed that by coming together to prepare their advocacy points and discuss their perspectives with the technical and financial partners, these young people demonstrate their determination to make their voices and aspirations heard in order to strengthen peace and social cohesion in their communities; said she remains convinced that the discussions during this workshop will be rich and fruitful, leading to the formulation of relevant and impactful advocacy points. “However, we remain very active in ensuring a smooth transition of support to young people in the North,” she promised, inviting participants to take full advantage of this workshop by establishing solid connections and lasting commitments with the other programmes and partners present.

a891.speaker: Trump administration
a891.name: Trump administration
a891.speech: Announced that it has chopped close to 130 million dollars from funds appropriated to support Ethiopia’s defence and counter-terrorism activities.

a1097.speaker: Mark Carney, Canadian Prime Minister
a1097.name: Mark Carney
a1097.title: Canadian Prime Minister
a1097.speech: Sharply criticised the Israeli government on Thursday, accusing it of not having prevented the rapid deterioration of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and of violating international law by refusing aid; on the platform X (formerly Twitter) insisted that Israeli control of aid distribution be replaced by a "full provision" of humanitarian aid managed by international organisations ; "Canada calls on all parties to negotiate an immediate ceasefire in good faith," declared Mr Carney; he reiterated the calls on Hamas to immediately release all hostages, and on the Israeli government to respect the territorial integrity of the West Bank and Gaza ; reaffirmed Canada's support for a two-State solution.

a1097.speaker: Anita Anand, Canadian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1097.name: Anita Anand
a1097.title: Canadian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a1097.speech: Described as "inexcusable" the lack of access to food and water for the women and children of Gaza, urging the Israeli government to "allow humanitarian aid to reach Palestinian civilians unimpeded, who are in urgent need of it" ; will take part in a United Nations conference on the two-State question next week in New York.

a1097.speaker: Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA)
a1097.name: Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA)
a1097.speech: Expressed its reservations, stating that Hamas does not want a ceasefire and is seeking to retain power.

a1097.speaker: Noah Shack, Director General of the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA)
a1097.name: Noah Shack
a1097.title: Director General of the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA)
a1097.speech: Declared that Hamas "thanks governments, including that of Canada, for their statements that encourage it to continue subjecting Gazans and Israelis to further suffering" ; recalled that at the NATO summit last month Mr Carney had underlined that a two-State solution requires Palestinian leaders to recognise Israel's right to live in security.

a1097.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a1097.name: Emmanuel Macron
a1097.title: French President
a1097.speech: Announced that his country would recognise Palestine as a State; in a post on X specified that this decision would be formalised at the United Nations General Assembly in September ; "The urgent thing today is that the war in Gaza cease and that the civilian population be saved," he wrote.

a1097.speaker: Group of some twenty countries including Canada, the United Kingdom, Japan and Australia (joint declaration)
a1097.name: Group of some twenty countries including Canada
a1097.title: the United Kingdom, Japan and Australia (joint declaration)
a1097.speech: Recently published a joint declaration calling for the immediate end of the war in Gaza.

a1097.speaker: Israeli parliament (Knesset)
a1097.name: Israeli parliament (Knesset)
a1097.speech: Approved on Wednesday a symbolic motion aimed at annexing the West Bank.

a1103.speaker: American analysts and experts (collectively, in exclusive statements to the Qatar News Agency)
a1103.name: American analysts and experts (collectively
a1103.title: in exclusive statements to the Qatar News Agency)
a1103.speech: Confirmed that the Israeli attack, which targeted the residential headquarters of several Hamas leaders in the Qatari capital, Doha, on Tuesday represents a "regrettable incident" and a clear violation of international norms ; stressed that targeting Qatar, a country that plays a key role in mediation, jeopardises diplomatic efforts in the region and represents a difficult test for the United States.

a1103.speaker: Dr Paul Davis, Vice-President for government business development at Securdam and founder and president of Jans Think International Security
a1103.name: Dr Paul Davis
a1103.title: Vice-President for government business development at Securdam and founder and president of Jans Think International Security
a1103.speech: Told QNA: "The attack on Doha was unexpected and the United States did not learn of it in time." He pointed out that this will "have serious consequences for Washington's relations with the Gulf states and for diplomacy concerning Gaza." ; Added: "The United States of America is working hard to preserve Qatar's key role as an essential and irreplaceable mediator. Doha has, through its credibility and effectiveness, proven that it is the only entity capable of fulfilling this role." He noted that this attack will "temporarily affect the image of the United States of America and its ability to coordinate with its partners in the Gulf."

a1103.speaker: Dr Thomas S. Warrick, nonresident senior fellow at the Scowcroft Middle East Security Initiative
a1103.name: Dr Thomas S. Warrick
a1103.title: nonresident senior fellow at the Scowcroft Middle East Security Initiative
a1103.speech: Said in a similar statement that the US position after the attack carried important messages, the most significant being "US President Donald Trump's promise to Qatar that such attacks will not be repeated" ; "Washington is determined to restart the mediation process with the participation of Qatar and Egypt, and we may see tangible steps in the coming days." ; "Targeting Doha represents a violation of international norms that prohibit harming mediators."

a1103.speaker: Chris Murphy, Democratic US Senator
a1103.name: Chris Murphy
a1103.title: Democratic US Senator
a1103.speech: Described the attack as "a clear violation of international law" ; said in public statements: "The Taliban and Hamas have political representation in Qatar because Doha has historically served as a mediator between these groups and legitimate states such as the United States of America and Israel, at the request of Washington itself." ; stated that Qatar is a key mediator and that people need to understand that the United States of America and Israel asked it to play that role, and what it received in return were airstrikes.

a1103.speaker: Robert Malley, former US envoy for Iran and former adviser on the Middle East to US President Barack Obama
a1103.name: Robert Malley
a1103.title: former US envoy for Iran and former adviser on the Middle East to US President Barack Obama
a1103.speech: Stated that the attack "confirms the Israeli government's lack of interest in achieving a negotiated end to the war in Gaza" ; "The attack poisons the environment for any country that wishes to mediate in the future," said in public statements, warning that the lack of broad political opposition within Israel reflects how "total destruction and unconditional surrender have become widely accepted policy."

a1124.speaker: Treatment Action Campaign (TAC), health advocacy organisation, and Sisonke, sex worker movement
a1124.name: Treatment Action Campaign (TAC)
a1124.title: health advocacy organisation, and Sisonke, sex worker movement
a1124.speech: Reported cases where sex workers — who used to get their treatment from US government-funded clinics where health workers were trained to address their reproductive health needs — have recently been turned away from state clinics or were denied condoms, at a Bhekisisa and Southern African HIV Clinicians Society webinar in May.

a1124.speaker: Bhekisisa's data team
a1124.name: Bhekisisa's data team
a1124.speech: Has found that people over 50 make up the second largest group of South Africa's HIV-positive population; twenty years ago, they were the smallest proportion.

a1124.speaker: Studies (cited)
a1124.name: Studies (cited)
a1124.speech: Have shown that people with HIV who are older than 50 have double the chance of having conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure too than what is seen in younger HIV-positive people.

a1124.speaker: Kate Rees, public health specialist with the Anova Health Institute
a1124.name: Kate Rees
a1124.title: public health specialist with the Anova Health Institute
a1124.speech: Said employing health workers to capture and manage health data will be a hard sell, during the Bhekisisa and the Southern African HIV Clinicians Society webinar — something that, for a public health issue that might be ignored because its fallout isn't immediately visible, could just make the problem so much worse.

a1124.speaker: Clinical HIV Research Unit, Wits University (press release)
a1124.name: Clinical HIV Research Unit
a1124.title: Wits University (press release)
a1124.speech: "This closure will significantly impact cervical cancer prevention efforts in SA, which faces one of the highest rates of cervical cancer in the world."

a1124.speaker: Clinical HIV Research Unit communication department, Wits University
a1124.name: Clinical HIV Research Unit communication department
a1124.title: Wits University
a1124.speech: "With timely screening and early detection being key to preventing cervical cancer, the closure of this screening unit at Helen Joseph Hospital leaves a major gap in services and will further strain the health service."

a1124.speaker: Francois Venter, HIV doctor and director of Ezintsha at the University of the Witwatersrand
a1124.name: Francois Venter
a1124.title: HIV doctor and director of Ezintsha at the University of the Witwatersrand
a1124.speech: "There's still the shame, stigma and moral issues that come with HIV."

a1124.speaker: Francois Venter, HIV doctor and director of Ezintsha at the University of the Witwatersrand
a1124.name: Francois Venter
a1124.title: HIV doctor and director of Ezintsha at the University of the Witwatersrand
a1124.speech: "If we went into the community aggressively looking for high sugar and blood pressure, we would do such a better job. Instead, we sit back and wait [until people turn up at clinics], which is why we do so badly with diabetes and hypertension." ; Says that when nurses have more work, they have less time to treat each patient, which makes it even harder to pick up NCDs: "Because of that, the actual interaction would take probably an hour and a half. When you've got a mile-long queue outside your door, you just don't have that time." ; "So they [nurses] go for the absolute basic stuff."

a1124.speaker: Health department data
a1124.name: Health department data
a1124.speech: According to health department data, Pepfar funded 2 320 nurses, of which just over half (those programmes that received their funds through USAid) have been laid off; Pepfar also funded 2 705 lay counsellors.

a1244.speaker: Souleymane Ouédraogo, National Director of Educo Benin
a1244.name: Souleymane Ouédraogo
a1244.title: National Director of Educo Benin
a1244.speech: “During this year 2019, a budget of approximately 787,200,000 CFA francs will be invested from our own funds in the development of projects and programmes in Benin. With 19 local partner NGOs in co-construction, 4 programmes will be implemented in Borgou, Alibori, Atlantique, Ouémé and Littoral.”

a1244.speaker: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a1244.name: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a1244.speech: As an organisation centred on children’s rights, Educo welcomes this initiative by UNESCO: “We share the conviction that if education is an end in itself, it is also the best means of guaranteeing rights, well-being and the dignity of life.” ; Stated that 75 million children and young people of school age worldwide need educational support, either at risk of losing their right to education or already deprived of it in countries facing war and violence, a situation largely explained by the fact that education is traditionally the least funded area of humanitarian aid, with less than 3% of total global funding.

a1244.speaker: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a1244.name: Educo Benin (organisation statement)
a1244.speech: Reaffirmed on the occasion of the International Day of Education its commitment to the exercise of children’s rights with a view to their well-being, undertaking to work alongside sister organisations, its local partners, the technical and decentralised services of the State, the communes, the communities and the children themselves for the achievement of lasting social change ; recalled that since 13 June 2018 Benin has had an education sector plan 2018-2030 (PSE), endorsed on 26 July 2018 by the technical and financial partners of the education sector and by civil society organisations, and that this international day is an opportunity to recall the need to unite energies for its effective operationalisation.

a1375.speaker: Ebson Uanguta, NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.name: Ebson Uanguta
a1375.title: NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.speech: Highlighted that the company has put in place strategies and policies to address its financial instability; while some of its debts have been paid, he added that the company still has a lot of work to do in ensuring it does not sink. "We need the suppliers of NAMCOR because we trade in oil. As we know, Namibia does not produce oil or petroleum products. We need to import this from other nations where oil is found. And when we import this, we trade it now in a domestic economy to supply the demand. And that is possibly where things went wrong, and hence NAMCOR found itself having significant debts. Because of that debt, we needed some kind of support from the government as shareholders. We really want to thank the government for coming in fully to support NAMCOR at that difficult time. They came up with a guarantee of N$1.2 billion; it was a sovereign guarantee, and the money was given by the commercial banks. So that has really enabled us somehow to stabilise the entity. It helped us to restructure some of our debts and almost brought us back to business."

a1375.speaker: Ebson Uanguta, NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.name: Ebson Uanguta
a1375.title: NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.speech: Acknowledges that the company stood to lose credibility with creditors and suppliers and says Namcor has had to re-strategise and come up with a recovery plan. "Part of that recovery plan was focused on how to stabilise the company and making sure to introduce efficiency measures to be able to ensure that there have been unnecessary expenses and that these expenses are contained and also strengthen the processes and bring about policies that are addressing some of the challenges that we found. Because in many cases, when companies governance lapses. It requires that some of the policies need to be re-updated or strengthened. So that whatever was done does not happen again."

a1375.speaker: Ebson Uanguta, NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.name: Ebson Uanguta
a1375.title: NAMCOR interim managing director
a1375.speech: Said income from recent oil discoveries in the Orange Basin, which are anticipated to become operational in the future, should greatly help in solving NAMCOR's cash flow troubles.

a1578.speaker: International relations and political analysts
a1578.name: International relations and political analysts
a1578.speech: Say President Lazarus Chakwera has been strong on foreign policy and that Malawi is benefitting from his diplomatic touch that also took him to several countries in what critics said is costly "globe-trotting"; the pundits pointed to trade, bilateral and multilateral relations, budgetary and off-budget support as areas shaped by Chakwera's foreign policy bona fides.

a1578.speaker: George Chaima, expert in government, public planning and international policy
a1578.name: George Chaima
a1578.title: expert in government, public planning and international policy
a1578.speech: Said in an interview that the opening of new diplomatic offices in Morocco, Israel and other countries has also helped Malawi to build stronger international bonds that are bearing fruits for its citizens; he said that apart from Israel getting into a labour export deal with Malawi, countries such as Morocco have been able to donate fertiliser, while others like Ukraine have donated maize. "We received fertiliser and food aid from some of them. It was through such trips that renewed confidence in foreign governments and international development agencies resumed or increased aid."

a1578.speaker: George Chaima, expert in government, public planning and international policy
a1578.name: George Chaima
a1578.title: expert in government, public planning and international policy
a1578.speech: Added that Chakwera's efforts to improve relations with neighbouring countries, especially Mozambique with which Malawi had frosty relations, particularly during the Bingu wa Mutharika era, has been significant: "Mozambique and Tanzania are our doors to the world. Being a landlocked country, it is absolutely important that the relationship with these two countries should remain sound."

a1578.speaker: Gift Sambo, University of Malawi (Unima) governance pundit
a1578.name: Gift Sambo
a1578.title: University of Malawi (Unima) governance pundit
a1578.speech: Noted that Mozambique is a very important country for Malawi's development: "Malawi has no choice, but to maintain strong ties with Maputo if it is to make headway in sectors such as energy, transport and infrastructure development. Being a landlocked country, it is consequential that the government should sustain good relations with Mozambique, which hosts vital sea ports on which Malawi is heavily dependent."

a1578.speaker: World Bank
a1578.name: World Bank
a1578.speech: In 2023, announced a resumption of direct budget support to the Malawi Government with a $137 million (about K237 billion) package to support local efforts to boost reforms and restore macro-economic stability.

a1578.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador
a1578.name: Rune Skinnebach
a1578.title: EU Ambassador
a1578.speech: Said during the signing of the 55 million euro finance agreement resuming direct budget support to Malawi: "today's agreement is a powerful symbol of renewed collaboration and commitment to our shared goals of stability, progress and inclusive development in Malawi."

a1578.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a1578.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a1578.title: President of Malawi
a1578.speech: Has boasted that in 2024 only, at least K300 billion was mobilised in off-budget support under his watch.

a1578.speaker: Michael Jana, University of Witwatersrand expert in State-society relations
a1578.name: Michael Jana
a1578.title: University of Witwatersrand expert in State-society relations
a1578.speech: Feels such aid is a positive development, but says more needs to be done to leverage the gains: "There has indeed been some progress in improving relations with donors. What is still missing though is harnessing that external financial and technical injection to develop an economy that is sustainable. Malawi is still dependent and cannot generate its own resources."

a1578.speaker: 2024 Africa Visa Openness Index (published data)
a1578.name: 2024 Africa Visa Openness Index (published data)
a1578.speech: Shows that Malawi has moved to position 22 this year from 25 out of 54 economies in 2019.

a1759.speaker: Participants at Martyrs Day commemorations by Eritrean diaspora nationals
a1759.name: Participants at Martyrs Day commemorations by Eritrean diaspora nationals
a1759.speech: Pledged to strengthen their engagement in supporting the Martyrs Trust Fund and the families of martyrs.

a1759.speaker: Eritrean nationals in Switzerland
a1759.name: Eritrean nationals in Switzerland
a1759.speech: Nationals who had previously taken on the responsibility of supporting families of martyrs reaffirmed their commitment.

a1759.speaker: Eritrean nationals residing in Dammam, Saudi Arabia
a1759.name: Eritrean nationals residing in Dammam
a1759.title: Saudi Arabia
a1759.speech: Have pledged to assume responsibility for supporting 11 families of martyrs.

a1864.speaker: U.S. Mission, Abuja (statement)
a1864.name: U.S. Mission
a1864.title: Abuja (statement)
a1864.speech: A statement made available to journalists on Friday said that the United States is committed to working with Nigeria in addressing security challenges.

a1864.speaker: David Greene, United States Charge d'affaires in Nigeria
a1864.name: David Greene
a1864.title: United States Charge d'affaires in Nigeria
a1864.speech: Stated that youth are the bedrock of society's social and economic development and that the future of Nigeria depends on youth charting a path of peace, as they are the future leaders of the great nation: "By attending today's conference, you've each signaled how important the cause of peace is for Nigeria...Youth are the bedrock of society's social and economic development. The future of Nigeria depends on youth charting a path of peace, as you are the future leaders of this great nation." ; "Our partnership harnesses the diverse strengths of its religious and traditional leaders, women, youth groups, government officials, and civil society. Through initiatives like USAID CIPP, the U.S. government is jointly identifying and promoting community-based solutions, empowering these groups to enhance community responses to challenges and build a resilient and peaceful future together."

a1897.speaker: Anderson Blanc, High Commissioner of Canada to Mozambique
a1897.name: Anderson Blanc
a1897.title: High Commissioner of Canada to Mozambique
a1897.speech: Expressed his deep honour in assuming this role and reaffirmed Canada's commitment to strengthening the longstanding friendship and cooperation between the two countries ; emphasized Canada's support for enhancing the environment for investment and economic cooperation, as well as strategic investments of overseas development assistance. He highlighted a particular ambition to expand bilateral trade and investment, particularly in sectors where Canadian expertise can contribute to Mozambique's development goals ; “It is a privilege to represent Canada in Mozambique, a country with which we share deep ties and common values. I look forward to working closely with the Government of Mozambique and our partners to advance our shared priorities and build a more prosperous, inclusive and sustainable future for our respective populations.” ; also noted the significance of 2025 as the year marking 50 years of diplomatic relations between Canada and Mozambique, a milestone that reflects the enduring strength of the bilateral partnership.

a1897.speaker: Daniel Francisco Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1897.name: Daniel Francisco Chapo
a1897.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1897.speech: Welcomed the High Commissioner and expressed appreciation for Canada's consistent partnership and support, particularly in areas that contribute to the well-being of Mozambican citizens.

a1897.speaker: Both parties (Canada and Mozambique)
a1897.name: Both parties (Canada and Mozambique)
a1897.speech: During the meeting, both parties underscored the importance of continued collaboration and partnership toward shared prosperity and security, in line with Mozambique's Five-Year Development Plan and Canada's new Africa Strategy.

a1926.speaker: Agricultural advisory council / scholastic body (agricultural researchers, higher institution lecturers, partners in the agricultural sector and scholars from abroad)
a1926.name: Agricultural advisory council / scholastic body (agricultural researchers
a1926.title: higher institution lecturers, partners in the agricultural sector and scholars from abroad)
a1926.speech: has criticized the close door approach the ministry has been practicing which they say alienates agricultural professionals; scholars were disappointed at the unstable organizational structure of the ministry; they said more attention needs to be paid to professionalism, and that the scant attention given to professionals in the field in favor of political appointees has led to tortoise like growth in the sector.

a1926.speaker: Oumer Hussein, Minister of Agriculture of Ethiopia
a1926.name: Oumer Hussein
a1926.title: Minister of Agriculture of Ethiopia
a1926.speech: "The ministry is in a strong position to produce enough wheat for its people." ; "The government shows high commitment to change this scenario by shifting to irrigation and making wheat import history."

a1926.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture data
a1926.name: Ministry of Agriculture data
a1926.speech: According to ministry data, the nation produced 4.6 million tons of wheat last fiscal year which makes Ethiopia the third largest producer of wheat in Africa next to Egypt and Morocco ; According to the ministry, only 2.1 million hectares of land are cultivated by irrigation.

a1926.speaker: FAO
a1926.name: FAO
a1926.speech: Small-scale farmers occupy 96% of the cropped area, while the remaining 4% are cropped by State farms and Producers' Cooperatives, according to FAO.

a1963.speaker: Ronnie Varkevisser, CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a1963.name: Ronnie Varkevisser
a1963.title: CEO of the Namibian Manufacturers Association (NMA)
a1963.speech: Reiterated the commitment of the NMA to continuing the partnership with USAID in staging the annual awards going forward, noting: “The Exporter awards are an important milestone in recognising the valuable work that export firms play in Namibia, and we are glad to partner with the USAID TradeHub in this regard and look forward to our future collaboration to grow the awards”.

a1994.speaker: US diplomats (telephone press conference)
a1994.name: US diplomats (telephone press conference)
a1994.speech: disclosed that the TPLF, who ignited the first fire on November 3 evening, had targeted to overthrow the central government and repossess the political spectrum; hinted that it’s their expectation that the operation will be done sooner; said that both sides were not willing to take part in mediation, which the US officials called a way for a goal not by itself an end of goal.

a1994.speaker: Tibor Nagy, US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.name: Tibor Nagy
a1994.title: US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.speech: on the TPLF’s motives: “I am not privy to the thinking of the TPLF leadership when they started this, but this was not to secede and create an independent state from Ethiopia, because the Ethiopian constitution has a provision for the states to be able to secede peacefully.” ; “I mean, again, it is difficult to tell the motivation, but it seems like they were doing this more to depose the prime minister from power and to reassert themselves into the prominent position that they had atop the Ethiopian political spectrum for the last 27 years.” ; “So hopefully right now I think that their tactic has had the opposite effect from what they were planning. It seems like this has brought the Ethiopian nation together, at least for the time being, in support of the prime minister, because this has really stoked Ethiopian nationalism, and hopefully those positive forces will remain.” ; “But again, I want to make it very clear that this is not about Tigray. There is no equivalency here. This is not two sovereign states fighting against each other. This is a faction of the government running a region in Ethiopia that has decided to undertake hostilities against the central government, and it has not – in my view – has had the effect that they thought that they were going to get.”

a1994.speaker: Tibor Nagy, US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.name: Tibor Nagy
a1994.title: US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.speech: on de-escalation and humanitarian access: “From the first attacks on November 3rd by the TPLF, on the Ethiopian National Defense Force bases in the Tigray region, we have publicly and privately highlighted our grave concern. We strongly urge an immediate de-escalation of tensions, a cessation of hostilities, and a return to peace.” ; “The protection and security of all civilians is essential. Our top priority is ensuring the welfare, protection, and security of U.S. citizens. The U.S. Embassy in Addis Ababa continues to work closely with the United Nations and others to relocate U.S. citizens in Tigray, as conditions permit.” ; “We also urge both sides to maintain access for humanitarian organizations to provide essential assistance to vulnerable groups in the region. We have been unequivocal with the Ethiopian Government and the TPLF on civilian lives since civilians must be protected and humanitarian access must be ensured.” ; said the United States continues to press the Ethiopian government to restore communication in the region as an act of accountability and transparency.

a1994.speaker: Tibor Nagy, US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.name: Tibor Nagy
a1994.title: US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.speech: on internationalisation of the conflict and attacks on civilians: “The TPLF leadership has admitted responsibility for the November 13 missile launches at airports in Bahir Dar and Gondar, in the Amhara region, and the November 14 attack in Eritrea. These unacceptable attacks make the situation more dangerous, and the Secretary condemned them in his most recent statement. We have been in contact with Eritrean Government officials and are urging their continued restraint.” ; “We remain deeply concerned over reports that civilians have been purposely targeted and attacked. We condemn the November 12 massacre in Mai-Kadra, apparently perpetrated by TPLF soldiers and militia as they retreated from the town.” ; “Those found responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law. Additionally, we are working with the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission and the Ethiopian government to ascertain why several journalists were recently arrested, their current status and well-being, and what charges they are facing.” ; “We expressed our thanks to Eritrea for not being provoked when they were attacked by missiles because apparently, one of the aims of the TPLF hardcore leadership was to try to internationalize the conflict so that there would be a way to try to really fan the flames of patriotism within the general population of Tigray, and we appreciate the fact that Eritrea has been restrained.” ; “Obviously, the Ethiopian government is also very keen to keep the situation from being internationalized because that would be destabilizing the entire region.”

a1994.speaker: Tibor Nagy, US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.name: Tibor Nagy
a1994.title: US Assistant Secretary for African Affairs
a1994.speech: on mediation: added that it is a tactic and a way to get to the goal that is a quick end to the conflict, restoration of peace, and protection of civilians. “A whole series of regional leaders, continental leaders, other international leaders have reached out with offers of mediation. At this point, neither party, from everything we hear, is interested in mediation.”

a1994.speaker: Michael Raynor, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1994.name: Michael Raynor
a1994.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1994.speech: said that both sides are not ready for negotiation, and stressed that the central government has grabbed support from regions and the general public: “Seemingly regional governments, federal governments, and large swaths of the people galvanizing around the government – the federal government and the national.”

a1994.speaker: Michael Raynor, US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1994.name: Michael Raynor
a1994.title: US Ambassador to Ethiopia
a1994.speech: on humanitarian access: “We, along with other humanitarian governments, including the United Nations, have been pressing from the outside: establishing humanitarian access for commodities – fuel, gas, other items; establishing a corridor to enable the insertion of those supplies and also to facilitate and monitor civilians. We raised that with the government. They said they would look into it.” ; “When I raised that with the TPLF, they did not really engage on that possibility. But we continue to press it very hard.” ; “Another aspect of this is that as the Ethiopian government continues to articulate a vision of the military conflict coming to an end fairly soon, a week or two from now, which isn’t to say that there isn’t a humanitarian crisis on the ground, because there absolutely is.”

a1994.speaker: TPLF chairman (Debretsion Gebremichael), interview with the Financial Times
a1994.name: TPLF chairman (Debretsion Gebremichael)
a1994.title: interview with the Financial Times
a1994.speech: argued that a breakup of Ethiopia could be one of the consequences of this conflict.

a1994.speaker: TPLF (via its media outlets and international media)
a1994.name: TPLF (via its media outlets and international media)

a1994.speaker: Tigray regional force leaders
a1994.name: Tigray regional force leaders
a1994.speech: have expressed their desire for negotiation.

a1994.speaker: Ethiopian government
a1994.name: Ethiopian government
a1994.speech: underlined that negotiation will happen when the mission is concluded and the target of the mission achieved.

a1994.speaker: Ethiopian government (to the US Ambassador)
a1994.name: Ethiopian government (to the US Ambassador)
a1994.speech: said they would look into establishing humanitarian access and a corridor for supplies.

a2027.speaker: Abdullahi Ali Ahmed (Wafow), Marka District Commissioner
a2027.name: Abdullahi Ali Ahmed (Wafow)
a2027.title: Marka District Commissioner
a2027.speech: According to him, the two main communities in Marka have joined hands and even united to defend their common interest as the people of Marka. "The trail of mistrust has now been changed by a joint trustful peace and safety committee formed by residents of Marka and sub-locations," Mr Wafow said.

a2027.speaker: Ibrahim Ali Adan Najah, Governor of Lower Shabelle Regional Administration
a2027.name: Ibrahim Ali Adan Najah
a2027.title: Governor of Lower Shabelle Regional Administration
a2027.speech: "Our people love one another. They share many things but the problem is that they did not communicate well to known each other's story and build trust. In fact if that could have been done longtime ago there could have been no problem," says the Governor, who officiated the training. ; "A community driven approach to understanding & providing security, such as this initiative, is key to the stabilisation efforts for the people of Lower Shabelle. They identify both causes of insecurity & solutions to it." ; "Thanks to the efforts we have made including the community driven approach, Marka has regained its status of one of Somalia's most peaceful, thriving urban city and its community is serving as an example that peace can be shaped by the locals through dialogue and trust."

a2027.speaker: Abdalla Bashir Nur, local elder
a2027.name: Abdalla Bashir Nur
a2027.title: local elder
a2027.speech: "Each clan believed that they were the owners of Marka and then fighting broke out. The once prosperous port city and surrounding area plunged into chaos, poverty and anarchy. No clan won. It is our common interest to live together as one. That is why we are here today for this safety and peace committee," Elder Abdalla Bashir Nur told the participants as he described the vivid memories of the horrors and suffering brought about by the conflict.

a2027.speaker: Muna Mohamed Subeyr, chairwoman of the local women organisation
a2027.name: Muna Mohamed Subeyr
a2027.title: chairwoman of the local women organisation
a2027.speech: Described the unity of Marka as the most important thing at stake for the whole community and said women are now playing a key role to ensure that any type of clan conflict does not return to Marka. "Many people, including women and children, were forced to flee Marka due to the hostility. Women were particularly vulnerable. We have a responsibility to take as the women of Marka. We will not allow anything that divides us."

a2053.speaker: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a2053.name: U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a2053.speech: Has confirmed conducting ten airstrikes in Somalia in 2025, as of March 5, following an inquiry from the American liberal think tank New America ; later clarified that three separate operations were carried out on February 20 against al-Shabaab, and later confirmed that two distinct operations had taken place on March 1.

a2053.speaker: Bihi Imaan Egeh, Somali Finance Minister
a2053.name: Bihi Imaan Egeh
a2053.title: Somali Finance Minister
a2053.speech: Disclosed that the U.S. had cut funding to the elite Danab special forces, a key counter-terrorism unit ; highlighted that this cutback, amounting to a significant loss in military funding, exacerbates Somalia's economic fragility, which is already strained by internal conflicts and global financial challenges.

a2086.speaker: Italian journalist (unnamed)
a2086.name: Italian journalist (unnamed)
a2086.speech: Asked the author by telephone during lunch how things were going in the city after the "coup d'etat."

a2086.speaker: Rahmane Idrissa, academic (described as a friend of the author)
a2086.name: Rahmane Idrissa
a2086.title: academic (described as a friend of the author)
a2086.speech: According to him, the intellectual class had long since disappeared.

a2262.speaker: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.name: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.speech: Has expressed support for President Arthur Peter Mutharika's administration and its commitment to restoring economic stability, predictability, and strong governance in Malawi ; Said it looks forward to partnering with the government and other key stakeholders to address prevailing macro-economic challenges.

a2262.speaker: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.name: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.speech: Highlighted the importance of attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) from major economies, including the United States and China, and said this would be critical for unlocking Malawi's growth potential and supporting meaningful economic recovery ; Said easing diplomatic hurdles could pave the way for dialogue on trade, economic development, and cooperation.

a2262.speaker: Philip Madinga, Chief Executive of Standard Bank Plc
a2262.name: Philip Madinga
a2262.title: Chief Executive of Standard Bank Plc
a2262.speech: Noted President Mutharika's determination to renew relations with the United States ; Observed that the departure of USAID had left gaps in development and technical support, which would require constructive engagement with international partners.

a2262.speaker: Arthur Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi (inaugural address)
a2262.name: Arthur Peter Mutharika
a2262.title: President of Malawi (inaugural address)
a2262.speech: Outlined the importance of attracting foreign direct investment from major economies, including the United States and China.

a2262.speaker: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.name: Standard Bank Plc
a2262.speech: Called for a strong public-private partnership during the government's transitional period ; Emphasized that fiscal discipline, good governance, and active dialogue with bilateral and multilateral donors and creditors are essential to set Malawi on a new economic trajectory.

a2459.speaker: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) (situation monitoring report)
a2459.name: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) (situation monitoring report)
a2459.speech: Warned that a humanitarian crisis is looming in Tigray Regional State and surrounding areas ; The report indicates significant civilian casualties, displacement, bodily harm, looting and property destruction in the areas investigated and urges immediate humanitarian assistance and support lest the situation spiral into a full-blown crisis ; They found that at least 31 civilians have died and 104 residences have been partially or completely destroyed in Bissober and Ullaga Kebeles in Chercher Wereda ; The report also detailed that most victims are still reliant on host communities for support and that many have only received one round of humanitarian assistance.

a2674.speaker: Mohamed Nor Indhos, Chief Executive Officer of Talla-Wadaag
a2674.name: Mohamed Nor Indhos
a2674.title: Chief Executive Officer of Talla-Wadaag
a2674.speech: "We have received a certificate of appreciation from the Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism of Somalia, this recognization to our services for our community here, encourages us to continue the social services" ; added that different parts of the Somali Community in Columbus, Ohio participated the event.

a2688.speaker: Ngaevarue Katjanga, Information ministry spokesperson
a2688.name: Ngaevarue Katjanga
a2688.title: Information ministry spokesperson
a2688.speech: Spelt out the ministry’s efforts to increase digital capacity in the country through digital strategies. “The government’s efforts to bridge the digital divide are clear through policy initiatives such as Universal Access, whose main objective is to ensure equitable access through subsidised infrastructure and services,” she said ; “Bridging the digital divide requires a concerted effort from the government, the business sector and communities. It is not only about laying cables or erecting network towers, but also about fostering an inclusive digital culture that empowers all citizens. Initiatives must go beyond infrastructure to include the development of digital skills, the provision of affordable access, and the creation of relevant local content that encourages community participation in the digital world.”

a2688.speaker: Ngaevarue Katjanga, Information ministry spokesperson (on persisting constraints)
a2688.name: Ngaevarue Katjanga
a2688.title: Information ministry spokesperson (on persisting constraints)
a2688.speech: Said that although the government has over the years collaborated with the private sector and continues to redouble efforts to expand broadband infrastructure networks to connect remote areas, schools and hospitals, insufficient telecommunications’ backhaul infrastructure in very remote rural areas and low digital literacy levels’ constraints persist.

a2688.speaker: Ngaevarue Katjanga, Information ministry spokesperson (on rural ICT centres)
a2688.name: Ngaevarue Katjanga
a2688.title: Information ministry spokesperson (on rural ICT centres)
a2688.speech: Stated that the ministry has proactively committed to address these challenges, ensuring that no community is left behind in the digital age through rural ICT centres (RICTCs), as digital technologies continue to evolve. “This means continually assessing and addressing the emerging needs and barriers to access, including the latest developments in technology,” the official added.

a2688.speaker: Ngaevarue Katjanga, Information ministry spokesperson (on MTC project)
a2688.name: Ngaevarue Katjanga
a2688.title: Information ministry spokesperson (on MTC project)
a2688.speech: Said another initiative to improve connectivity is MTC’s “081 Every1” telecommunications project which provides network coverage to every citizen of the country.

a2688.speaker: 2023 housing and population census report
a2688.name: 2023 housing and population census report
a2688.speech: Stated that 34.9% of households in Namibia have access to mobile internet connectivity. In urban and rural areas, 50.3% and 16.2% of households, respectively, had access to mobile internet connectivity. About 52% of the population above the age of three own a mobile phone, with 28.5% of those being smartphones.

a2688.speaker: Namibia Statistics Agency
a2688.name: Namibia Statistics Agency
a2688.speech: Reported that 93% of the population has access to telecommunications networks.

a2688.speaker: Harambee Prosperity Plan
a2688.name: Harambee Prosperity Plan
a2688.speech: Highlights the challenges faced by the country, despite the search for solutions. This includes the unavailability of electricity infrastructure in semi-urban and remote rural areas, hindering both the provision and uptake of ICT services.

a2694.speaker: Embassy of Japan in Djibouti
a2694.name: Embassy of Japan in Djibouti
a2694.speech: Stated that on the occasion of the embassy's 10th anniversary it wished to look back on the history of the deepening ties between Japan and Djibouti, noting that nearly 200 development projects have been carried out and nearly 80 billion DJF and 60 economic cooperation projects were provided up to 2020 ; Said that although piracy incidents in the region have decreased considerably, “we will continue to work to protect the security of maritime traffic, which handles 80% of global logistics” ; Said Japan remains with Djibouti during the COVID-19 health situation, providing vaccines through COVAX and various projects through the United Nations ; Said “The Government of Japan will continue to work with the government as an equal and sincere partner for the next 10 years and beyond.”

a2694.speaker: Abe Shinzo, former Prime Minister of Japan
a2694.name: Abe Shinzo
a2694.title: former Prime Minister of Japan
a2694.speech: During his 2013 visit to Djibouti and talks with President Ismail Omar Guelleh, he expressed his gratitude for the cooperation and support of the Djiboutian government for the anti-piracy operation and for the solidarity shown following the great earthquake in Japan.

a2836.speaker: US government, under the leadership of Donald Trump
a2836.name: US government
a2836.title: under the leadership of Donald Trump
a2836.speech: recently announced a cut of over 83% in external funding provided by USAID.

a2836.speaker: Sumaiya Ibraimo, humanitarian assistant of the Association of Young Promoters of Participatory Citizenship
a2836.name: Sumaiya Ibraimo
a2836.title: humanitarian assistant of the Association of Young Promoters of Participatory Citizenship
a2836.speech: reports: "With the suspension [imposed by the Trump administration], we were forced to interrupt our activities, as we could not carry them out without funding. Currently, we are only maintaining actions that do not require large resources."

a2836.speaker: Sumaiya Ibraimo, humanitarian assistant of the Association of Young Promoters of Participatory Citizenship
a2836.name: Sumaiya Ibraimo
a2836.title: humanitarian assistant of the Association of Young Promoters of Participatory Citizenship
a2836.speech: says it is difficult to establish new partnerships in the short term: "Right now, our hands are tied. Most of the activities we were developing require immediate resources. As a non-profit organization, we do not have the capacity to sustain these actions without external support."

a2836.speaker: Forum of Non-Governmental Organizations of Cabo Delgado (FOCADE)
a2836.name: Forum of Non-Governmental Organizations of Cabo Delgado (FOCADE)
a2836.speech: warns that the cuts made by the US administration will directly affect the province's vulnerable population.

a2836.speaker: Frederico Joao, FOCADE president
a2836.name: Frederico Joao
a2836.title: FOCADE president
a2836.speech: expresses concern about the situation: "It is devastating. At a time when Cabo Delgado, Nampula and part of Zambezia were simultaneously hit by a cyclone, the cut in humanitarian aid by the new US administration is extremely painful." ; notes that the cut puts many humanitarian workers at risk of unemployment: "The impact is not limited to the beneficiaries of the assistance. The humanitarian agents themselves, who depend on these projects for their livelihood, are also affected. This means that, in addition to the humanitarian impact, there will be a severe social effect with the increase in unemployment."

a2836.speaker: Frederico Joao, FOCADE president
a2836.name: Frederico Joao
a2836.title: FOCADE president
a2836.speech: suggests seeking new funders to reduce dependence on US aid: "We must try to forget about US aid for a while, which is considerably larger than that of other donors. We should explore, for example, the support of the European Union and other development agencies, such as UKAID, to ensure the continuity of assistance to vulnerable populations" ; also argues that, in a difficult scenario, internal solidarity should be strengthened, recommending that Mozambique increase production to reduce the need for external assistance.

a2836.speaker: Gafuro, president of the Kwendeleya Association
a2836.name: Gafuro
a2836.title: president of the Kwendeleya Association
a2836.speech: charges that a significant part of the resources has not been effectively directed to the populations in need: "Many institutions ended up spending more money on administrative costs than on implementing projects. This compromised the effectiveness of the assistance. The problem is not [only] with the government, but also with the organizations that received the funds and do not know how to apply them properly."

a2836.speaker: Minister of Finance of Mozambique
a2836.name: Minister of Finance of Mozambique
a2836.speech: Speaking after a meeting held on Friday (14.03) with the US ambassador in Maputo, warned that the suspension of USAID funds would affect the 2025 state budget proposal.

a2918.speaker: Richard M. Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2918.name: Richard M. Mills Jr.
a2918.title: US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2918.speech: Clarified the current status of US assistance to Nigeria, stating that a 90-day pause has been implemented by the new administration to review and improve the effectiveness of the assistance, and emphasized that no assistance has been cut yet and no decisions have been made about the future of US assistance to Nigeria: “Let me clarify one thing. Right now, the new administration has put in a 90 day pause on our assistance. No assistance has been cut yet, no decisions have been made about the future of our assistance. In fact, Secretary Rubio has said this is not about ending foreign assistance to our partners and friends like Nigeria. It’s about how to make the assistance more effective and how to make sure that it aligns with US government policies and interests. So that’s what this 90 day pause is for... but I think many of you have seen I hope that there are waivers, waivers for our assistance that’s life saving, that provides humanitarian life saving assistance, whether that’s to HIV patients or to mother and child nutrition needs or to internally displaced people. So that that continues, where we’ll be in 90 days, we will know. Thank you very much.”

a2918.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (cited by Ambassador Mills)
a2918.name: Marco Rubio
a2918.title: US Secretary of State (cited by Ambassador Mills)
a2918.speech: Has said this is not about ending foreign assistance to partners and friends like Nigeria; it’s about how to make the assistance more effective and how to make sure that it aligns with US government policies and interests.

a2918.speaker: Richard M. Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2918.name: Richard M. Mills Jr.
a2918.title: US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2918.speech: Outlined four key priorities for the coming years aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and promoting development in Nigeria: the first is to enhance the business environment, fostering increased trade and investment between the US and Nigeria; the second is fighting corruption and promoting transparency and accountability in Nigeria — “The US Embassy will support Nigerian voices advocating for greater transparency and good governance. The third priority involves increasing engagement at the state and local levels, working closely with governing authorities to develop programs and assistance that address local needs. The fourth priority builds on the success of existing healthcare programs, which have contributed significantly to reducing HIV cases and eradicating polio in Nigeria. The US Embassy aims to transition these programs, ensuring sustainability and continued impact.”

a2918.speaker: Richard M. Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a2918.name: Richard M. Mills Jr.
a2918.title: US Ambassador to Nigeria
