a2918.speech: Said the United States has implemented robust policies and procedures to prevent any diversion of its assistance funding to terrorist groups like Boko Haram in Nigeria, covering funding from USAID, the Department of Defense and the State Department, and assured that the safeguards are designed to guarantee that US aid does not inadvertently end up financing terrorist activities: “Let me be clear, there’s no friend of Nigeria that has been stronger and its condemnation of the violence of Boko Haram and Boko Haram contempt for human life than the United States. We have labeled Boko Haram since 2013 a foreign terrorist organization... I can assure you, have policies and procedures in place to ensure that USAID funding, any of our assistance funding, whether it comes from USAID, the Department of Defense, the State Department, is not diverted to a terrorist group like Boko Haram. There is absolutely no evidence that I have seen that that has occurred, and certainly if we ever had evidence presented to us that a program funding was being diverted to Boko Haram we would immediately investigate along with our Nigerian partners. And so I just want to be clear that when it comes to Boko Haram the United States stands with Nigeria and wanting to rid this country of the scourge that that organization represents.”

a3064.speaker: H.E. Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union (AU) Commission
a3064.name: H.E. Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a3064.title: Chairperson of the African Union (AU) Commission
a3064.speech: Seized the opportunity to voice deep concerns regarding recent global aid cuts and the persistent failure to fulfill climate finance pledges made to African nations.

a3064.speaker: Bill Gates, Co-Chair and Trustee of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
a3064.name: Bill Gates
a3064.title: Co-Chair and Trustee of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
a3064.speech: Reportedly echoed these sentiments, acknowledging the disproportionate and unfair treatment Africa faces in global climate discussions, despite its minimal contribution to greenhouse gas emissions; in response, committed to advocating for sustained international aid and fostering deeper, more equitable partnerships to address these disparities.

a3064.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, AU Commission Chairperson, and Bill Gates (jointly)
a3064.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a3064.title: AU Commission Chairperson, and Bill Gates (jointly)
a3064.speech: Emphasized the urgent need for global solidarity in addressing pressing challenges and jointly reaffirmed the critical importance of fair trade practices, substantial debt relief for African economies, and robust investment in African-led innovation, governance structures, and resilience-building efforts.

a3106.speaker: National Association of Shea Processors of Benin (ANTK-Benin) (press release, signed by president Gilles Roger Adamon)
a3106.name: National Association of Shea Processors of Benin (ANTK-Benin) (press release
a3106.title: signed by president Gilles Roger Adamon)
a3106.speech: Expresses its satisfaction at the increase in the export tax on shea nuts: “This commendable decision goes in the right direction and will allow local processors, who now have sufficient production capacity to process all of Benin’s shea nut output, to obtain supplies at a reasonable price — the only condition for Benin’s shea butter to be competitive on the world market.” ; “For this beneficial initiative for our country’s shea sector, ANTK very sincerely thanks the government of Benin, through the Minister of Industry and Trade as well as the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries.”

a3313.speaker: Benjamin Herzberg, World Bank expert, senior private sector specialist and co-manager of the project
a3313.name: Benjamin Herzberg
a3313.title: World Bank expert, senior private sector specialist and co-manager of the project
a3313.speech: Explained that this project, financed by the World Bank, is intended to support more than 6,000 young people and women wishing to go into entrepreneurship: “This project will strive to support aspiring entrepreneurs by facilitating their access to training, to strengthen and develop essential services for businesses so as to make them more readily accessible, and to help entrepreneurs identify and integrate into competitive value chains” ; “Offering young people and women future prospects through training in entrepreneurial skills can lead them to become aware of their capacity to act. This develops a sense of belonging that fosters the resilience of their communities.”

a3313.speaker: Oubah Ahmed Malow, Director General of the Centre for Leadership and Entrepreneurship (CLE)
a3313.name: Oubah Ahmed Malow
a3313.title: Director General of the Centre for Leadership and Entrepreneurship (CLE)
a3313.speech: Gave a broad presentation on the concept of the Entrepreneurial Ecosystem, which is made up of three main factors: “First of all, the existence of a critical mass of entrepreneurs, companies and specialised institutions in the same environment. Then, secondly, a dense network of relationships between the different actors, and a corporate culture that brings these groups together” ; on the life phases of a company: “This phase requires support for the initiative in order to awaken one’s creative spirit and pique one’s curiosity. Then, ideation, which consists of a phase during which the idea of creation takes shape and needs modelling” ; “This phase requires support through training programmes and an approach aimed at transmitting know-how” ; concluded with a comparative study of the Tunisian ecosystem, which appears well developed with more than 157 actors.

a3324.speaker: Nozipho Mlotshwa, 32, South African lab technician, Antiviral Gene Therapy Research Unit, Wits University
a3324.name: Nozipho Mlotshwa
a3324.title: 32, South African lab technician, Antiviral Gene Therapy Research Unit, Wits University
a3324.speech: “This was very exciting. We were getting quite good results,” Mlotshwa told Reuters in the lab.

a3324.speaker: US State Department
a3324.name: US State Department
a3324.speech: The US state department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

a3324.speaker: Patrick Arbuthnot, director of the Antiviral Gene Therapy Research Unit
a3324.name: Patrick Arbuthnot
a3324.title: director of the Antiviral Gene Therapy Research Unit
a3324.speech: “We were gaining momentum,” adding: “An HIV vaccine is the Holy Grail of the field.”

a3324.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3324.name: Donald Trump
a3324.title: US President
a3324.speech: In January, Trump ordered a 90-day pause in all foreign development assistance, pending assessment of its consistency with his America First foreign policy; separately, he has targeted South Africa with an executive order to cut all funding to the country, citing disapproval of its land reform policy and its genocide case against US ally Israel.

a3324.speaker: Ntobeko Ntusi, CEO of the SA Medical Research Council
a3324.name: Ntobeko Ntusi
a3324.title: CEO of the SA Medical Research Council
a3324.speech: Said he did not expect funding for projects such as Brilliant to resume, given the executive order on aid to South Africa.

a3324.speaker: Nigel Garrett, Chief scientific officer of the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a3324.name: Nigel Garrett
a3324.title: Chief scientific officer of the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation
a3324.speech: Said the shot that was ready for testing on humans was a mix of two vaccine substances developed in the US and the Netherlands, which have shown promise but never been tested together, and are now in storage ; “We had a huge opportunity and good funding. It’s difficult for other funders to fill that gap.”

a3448.speaker: Portugal com ACNUR, national partner of UNHCR (press statement)
a3448.name: Portugal com ACNUR
a3448.title: national partner of UNHCR (press statement)
a3448.speech: "By the end of 2024, it is estimated that more than 65 million people from all regions of Africa will be forced to flee in search of protection and humanitarian assistance. A figure that represents almost half (49%) of the total number of displaced people in the world" ; stresses that "underfunding emerges as the main threat to humanitarian aid" ; highlights the situation in Mozambique, where "the escalation of armed violence at the end of last year caused a new wave of forced displacement, with around 113,000 people forced to flee and leave everything behind. Not forgetting that currently around 822,000 people still remain displaced in this country."

a3448.speaker: Joana Feliciano, head of Marketing and Communication at Portugal com ACNUR
a3448.name: Joana Feliciano
a3448.title: head of Marketing and Communication at Portugal com ACNUR
a3448.speech: Says that "the many conflicts and situations of armed violence that have erupted over the last decade on the continent and the growing impact of climate change have forced all those people and their families to leave everything behind" ; adds that "From the Sahel to the Horn of Africa, not forgetting the central and southern regions of the continent, both displaced people and host communities are living in an extreme situation. New conflicts, greater competition for resources due to the effects of climate change, poverty and inflation are escalating humanitarian needs."

a3448.speaker: UNHCR (UN refugee agency)
a3448.name: UNHCR (UN refugee agency)
a3448.speech: Forecasts that in the East and Horn of Africa region alone, by the end of 2024 some 23.6 million forcibly displaced and stateless people will be hosted, mainly due to the conflicts in Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia and the DRC and to floods and droughts caused by climate change; projects 12.2 million forcibly displaced, returned and stateless people in Southern Africa, a 9% increase to 13.6 million in West and Central Africa, and 15.8 million in North Africa by the end of the year.

a3491.speaker: Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (Zimstat), July 2025 Trade and Price Statistics Report
a3491.name: Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (Zimstat)
a3491.title: July 2025 Trade and Price Statistics Report
a3491.speech: Zimstat said tobacco and semi-manufactured gold led Zimbabwe's export portfolio in June, helping drive total export earnings to US$723.5 million for the month. According to the report, semi-manufactured gold accounted for 53.6 percent of exports, followed by nickel mattes (12.7 percent), and partly or wholly stemmed/stripped tobacco (5.7 percent).

a3491.speaker: Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (Zimstat)
a3491.name: Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency (Zimstat)
a3491.speech: Pointed out that Zimbabwe's trade partners remain largely consistent, with exports heavily concentrated in a few key markets namely the United Arab Emirates at the top of the list of destinations, taking in 54.8 percent of goods, followed by South Africa (23.5 percent) and China (8.3 percent).

a3651.speaker: William Tunzine, administrator (Ilha de Moçambique)
a3651.name: William Tunzine
a3651.title: administrator (Ilha de Moçambique)
a3651.speech: According to him, there are reports of people [stranded], particularly on Mozambique Island, while those in the same situation in Angoche have already been rescued.

a3651.speaker: Luísa Meque, president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.name: Luísa Meque
a3651.title: president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.speech: Called for caution in crossings so that those stranded do not risk their lives ; “This is a major challenge; we want to appeal to the people who are stranded to avoid making the crossing because of the scale of the cuts that exist. It is important that they do not cross without safety, because that could endanger their lives.”

a3651.speaker: Luísa Meque, president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.name: Luísa Meque
a3651.title: president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.speech: Promised to remain in Nampula in the coming hours while intense humanitarian aid operations are under way for the 19,602 families, preliminary figures, affected ; confirmed the number of deaths and injuries, noting the data are being updated: “From the preliminary survey carried out up to this morning, we count six deaths, one in Larde, another in Meconta and four in Nacala. These are the deaths confirmed by Health; there are twenty injured. These are preliminary data, the teams are still in the field working. We will update this information and, in the coming hours, it may change.”

a3651.speaker: Luísa Meque, president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.name: Luísa Meque
a3651.title: president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD)
a3651.speech: According to her, the frequent occurrence of cyclones in this part of the country, exceeding weather forecasts, is a factor that increases the pressure on the government for humanitarian assistance to families, a reality one must learn to live with.

a3651.speaker: Eduardo Abdula, Governor of Nampula
a3651.name: Eduardo Abdula
a3651.title: Governor of Nampula
a3651.speech: Asked for speed in carrying out the work and in opening a detour so the congestion can be cleared ; “What I asked of the contractors and the National Roads Administration is that they try to do this in the shortest possible time, that they work day and night. You saw the flow of cars stopped there, people and goods, and we run the risk that, if this continues, there will be supply problems in the city of Nampula.” ; expressed considerable concern about reports of problems in other districts caused by the intense rain that accompanied “Jude”.

a3651.speaker: INAM (National Institute of Meteorology)
a3651.name: INAM (National Institute of Meteorology)
a3651.speech: Forecasts weak to moderate rains, locally heavy, accompanied by thunderstorms and moderate winds, which may at times blow in gusts; precipitation could be between 10 and 50 millimetres in 24 hours, and an improvement in the weather in Nampula province from Friday.

a3879.speaker: Federal transport officials (Ethiopia)
a3879.name: Federal transport officials (Ethiopia)
a3879.speech: Officials say the mandatory quota is prompted by the need to transport fertiliser that has been sitting in Djibouti since January this year.

a3879.speaker: Mohammed Kibret, general manager, Alpha Cross-Border Freight Transport Owners' Association
a3879.name: Mohammed Kibret
a3879.title: general manager, Alpha Cross-Border Freight Transport Owners' Association
a3879.speech: Raises concerns about potential delays in the loading and unloading process. “Officials have promised eased loading procedures,” he said. “But we haven’t seen any improvements.” ; “Some of the destinations are also difficult to drive to. This is why some of the tariffs are set higher.”

a3879.speaker: Industry players / many in the trucking industry
a3879.name: Industry players / many in the trucking industry
a3879.speech: Many in the industry complain about the "clunky" loading and unloading process; industry players say it can take a truck up to three weeks on average to complete a single trip, inflating operational costs.

a3879.speaker: Dereje Legesse, general manager, Segon Cross Border Freight Transport Owners' Association
a3879.name: Dereje Legesse
a3879.title: general manager, Segon Cross Border Freight Transport Owners' Association
a3879.speech: Says the tariffs are no different from market prices. “Although the tariff seems higher in some cases, it's similar when calculated for a kilometre.”

a3879.speaker: Federal officials (Ethiopia)
a3879.name: Federal officials (Ethiopia)
a3879.speech: Officials say the activities of the trucks will be monitored at four checkpoints.

a3879.speaker: Bareo Hassen, State Minister for Transport & Logistics
a3879.name: Bareo Hassen
a3879.title: State Minister for Transport & Logistics
a3879.speech: "Failure to comply with the rules will have serious consequences,” warns Bareo Hassen.

a3879.speaker: Bareo Hassen, State Minister for Transport & Logistics
a3879.name: Bareo Hassen
a3879.title: State Minister for Transport & Logistics
a3879.speech: Disclosed that officials are expecting two other vessels carrying wheat and fertiliser to call ports in Djibouti in the coming weeks.

a3879.speaker: Matiwos Ensermu (PhD), associate professor of logistics and supply chain management, Addis Abeba University School of Commerce
a3879.name: Matiwos Ensermu (PhD)
a3879.title: associate professor of logistics and supply chain management, Addis Abeba University School of Commerce
a3879.speech: Experts caution federal authorities to explore other alternatives instead of playing it tough with truck owners; according to Matiwos, they can use the Ethio-Djibouti Railway efficiently.

a3942.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.name: Yusuph Mwenda
a3942.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.speech: “We must invest more in technology-driven reforms. I’m pleased that you will be discussing how best we can leverage artificial intelligence in tax administration. This is the best way to apply science in raising voluntary tax compliance” ; said that technology, particularly AI, offers practical, forward-looking solutions to challenges such as tax evasion and smuggling, enabling smarter tax collection and more effective taxpayer engagement.

a3942.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.name: Yusuph Mwenda
a3942.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.speech: While acknowledging progress in expanding the tax base and improving compliance, pointed to persisting obstacles such as discriminatory tariffs that violate regional integration protocols and the complexity of tax systems: “Discriminatory fiscal measures within our region contradict efforts toward harmonisation and integration,” calling for stronger collaboration to eliminate these barriers and foster seamless trade.

a3942.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.name: Yusuph Mwenda
a3942.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.speech: Urged taxpayers to take an active role in promoting compliance by demanding fiscal receipts: “Those who fail to issue receipts undermine our collective efforts to build a culture of voluntary compliance,” adding that TRA will launch a public awareness campaign across Dar es Salaam to encourage proper receipt issuance.

a3942.speaker: Yusuph Mwenda, Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.name: Yusuph Mwenda
a3942.title: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) Commissioner General
a3942.speech: Advocated for simplifying tax laws to create a more predictable and user-friendly system: “We need a tax system so simple that even a Form Four leaver can comply with it.”

a3942.speaker: Beatus Nchota, Chairperson of the East Africa Revenue Administration Technical Committee
a3942.name: Beatus Nchota
a3942.title: Chairperson of the East Africa Revenue Administration Technical Committee
a3942.speech: Applauded the forum’s role in fostering regional cooperation and setting the stage for the upcoming Commissioners-General meeting in Rwanda, and urged members to remain proactive and focused on solutions that advance the region’s shared goals of economic transformation and prosperity.

a3942.speaker: Beatus Nchota, Chairperson of the East Africa Revenue Administration Technical Committee
a3942.name: Beatus Nchota
a3942.title: Chairperson of the East Africa Revenue Administration Technical Committee
a3942.speech: “As East Africa’s economies grow, so too must our tax systems—by embracing innovation, including AI and data analytics to meet the demands of a modern economy.”

a3991.speaker: Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG)
a3991.name: Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama
a3991.title: Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG)
a3991.speech: Admitted that the proposed utility tariff hikes put forward by power producers and distributors could weigh heavily on its next policy rate decision if approved ; “On the fiscal side, execution in the first half of 2025 signalled consolidation: the deficit on a commitment basis was contained at 0.7 percent of GDP, below target, contributing, together with cedi strength and external restructuring, to a decline in the public debt ratio by mid-year. Against this backdrop of easing inflation pressures, anchored expectations, and stronger buffers, the MPC in July reduced the policy rate by 300 basis points to 25.0 percent” ; added that while there are encouraging signs of fiscal stability, global trade risks and the looming tariff hikes will be critical in shaping the next policy stance ; “While reiterating our readiness to adjust as the disinflation process evolves and risks, such as global trade disruptions or prospective utility tariff adjustments, are assessed, our commitment remains firm: maintain price stability, safeguard financial stability, and create the conditions for inclusive, sustainable growth.”

a3991.speaker: Utility providers (power and water producers and distributors)
a3991.name: Utility providers (power and water producers and distributors)
a3991.speech: Have requested increases of more than 200% in both water and electricity tariffs, raising concerns that such adjustments could reverse recent progress in lowering inflation.

a4099.speaker: Rob Rosenbaum, former USAID economist
a4099.name: Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.title: former USAID economist
a4099.speech: “We called ourselves the lifeboat crew at the beginning. The ship has been sinking, and there aren’t enough lifeboats for every project to get on, and so we’re trying to literally save as many babies as we can, get as many on to these lifeboats as possible, via the projects that are delivering aid.” ; terms the dates on which projects would collapse “drop-dead dates”; says he and colleagues were approached by a foundation that “wanted to figure out how they could make the best use of their limited resources”, and that they created a menu from the list of cancelled projects, identifying those “delivering the most life-saving aid per dollar”.

a4099.speaker: Rob Rosenbaum, former USAID economist
a4099.name: Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.title: former USAID economist
a4099.speech: On the funders: “They come from very different reasons and perspectives, but the common thread that we’ve heard from them is, ‘I feel horrified by what’s going on. I really want to figure out a way to step in.’”

a4099.speaker: Rob Rosenbaum, former USAID economist
a4099.name: Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.title: former USAID economist
a4099.speech: “I think that there was an ‘aha’ moment for all of us as we started working on this, that this created an opportunity to pivot from the ice-cream on the couch, wallowing in the misery of everything that was happening around us, to having something productive to really sink our teeth into.”

a4099.speaker: Rob Rosenbaum, former USAID economist
a4099.name: Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.title: former USAID economist
a4099.speech: Says it is vital to keep such programmes going, not only because restarting operations if they stopped would be hugely expensive but also because of how much trust would be lost in the conflict-ravaged areas if Alima withdrew.

a4099.speaker: Alliance for International Medical Action (Alima), via Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.name: Alliance for International Medical Action (Alima)
a4099.title: via Rob Rosenbaum
a4099.speech: “Alima told us […] ‘we’re very worried that if we walk away, we may never be invited back.’”

a4099.speaker: Project Resource Optimization (Pro) team
a4099.name: Project Resource Optimization (Pro) team
a4099.speech: Estimates the saved projects will benefit 40 million people, including many children under five.

a4099.speaker: Project Resource Optimization (Pro)
a4099.name: Project Resource Optimization (Pro)
a4099.speech: Says that, having found funding for all projects on its initial list, it will now focus on reaching more people with “proven, cost-effective interventions”; it does not seek to save the projects indefinitely but to “buy time for the organisations and, frankly, the broader ecosystem, to figure out a longer-term solution”.

a4120.speaker: Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Media, Information and Broadcasting Services (report presented in National Assembly)
a4120.name: Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Media
a4120.title: Information and Broadcasting Services (report presented in National Assembly)
a4120.speech: Stressed that the Treasury should provide financial support to the responsible Ministry, especially in securing foreign currency required to procure digital transmitters: “Progress has been visible, with eighteen transmission sites successfully transitioning to digital. However, delays in funding disbursements and a lack of adequate financial resources have slowed further advancements. It is crucial for the Ministry of Finance, Economic Development, and Investment Promotion to prioritize the project’s financing.”

a4120.speaker: Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Media, Information and Broadcasting Services (report presented in National Assembly)
a4120.name: Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Media
a4120.title: Information and Broadcasting Services (report presented in National Assembly)
a4120.speech: Recommended that the Ministry of Finance exempt set-top boxes from import duties to improve affordability: “The committee further suggests that decoders be made widely available in retail outlets, including electronics stores and large chains like TV Sales and Hire. This would ensure the decoders are accessible to all Zimbabweans. Allowing the Broadcasting Authority of Zimbabwe (BAZ) to expand its retail operations would also empower local businesses, while BAZ continues its regulatory role.”

a4138.speaker: Time magazine
a4138.name: Time magazine
a4138.speech: “Donald Trump’s Disruption is Back…He’s Back”, with an illustration showing President Biden’s aviator sunglasses being swiped off the Resolute Desk.

a4138.speaker: A body language expert (unnamed)
a4138.name: A body language expert (unnamed)
a4138.speech: Has observed that the simple language of the picture is that Trump is on a revenge mission.

a4138.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (Truth Social posts)
a4138.name: Donald Trump
a4138.title: US President (Truth Social posts)
a4138.speech: Has promised that he will “make heads spin on his first day back in office” ; posted memes on Truth Social, including one that says: “Not elected to be nice. Elected to get results.”

a4138.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (inaugural speech)
a4138.name: Donald Trump
a4138.title: US President (inaugural speech)
a4138.speech: Accused the democrats of a horrible betrayal of our people. “All of this will change starting today,” he bellowed. He threatened to change the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America, and take back the Panama Canal, which he called “a foolish gift” to Panama. He declared that he would be “a peacemaker and a unifier,” and that under his watch, America will be the most respected nation in the world ; “There are only two genders – male and female, and that will be US state policy, and those who rejected COVID mandate will be reinstated with full back pay.” ; said he wants to overhaul America’s trade system and impose tariffs and taxes to “enrich our country” by setting up an External Revenue Service ; “And we will begin the process of returning millions and millions of criminal aliens back to the places from which they came.” ; said he will “direct all members of my cabinet… to defeat what was record inflation” ; promised what he called “the revolution of common sense” ; “From this moment on, the decline of America is over… I return to the Presidency confident and optimistic that we are at the start of a thrilling new era of national success. A tide of change is sweeping the country. Sunlight is pouring over the entire world. And America has the chance to seize this opportunity like never before” ; insisted in a second speech that he won the election in 2020.

a4138.speaker: Amy Klobuchar, US Senator (D-Minnesota), chairwoman of the Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural ceremonies
a4138.name: Amy Klobuchar
a4138.title: US Senator (D-Minnesota), chairwoman of the Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural ceremonies
a4138.speech: In declaring the ceremonies open and welcoming everyone, talked again and again about “peaceful transfer of power at the heart of our democracy”, our enduring democracy, and how the “Capitol is the people’s home”, and the responsibility of citizenship not to seek malice.

a4138.speaker: Deb Fischer, US Senator (R-Nebraska)
a4138.name: Deb Fischer
a4138.title: US Senator (R-Nebraska)
a4138.speech: Made the additional point about “the prominence of a people through change.”

a4138.speaker: Elon Musk, businessman
a4138.name: Elon Musk
a4138.title: businessman
a4138.speech: Told the audience at the Capital One Arena that Trump’s win is “no ordinary win, this was a fork in the road of human civilisation” and that “the future of civilisation is assured” ; echoed Trump’s sentiment that now is the time “to plant the Stripes and Stars on the planet Mars.”

a4138.speaker: Jose Raul Mulino, President of Panama
a4138.name: Jose Raul Mulino
a4138.title: President of Panama
a4138.speech: Says he must “comprehensively reject the words of President Donald Trump“ because “the canal is and will remain Panama’s.”

a4217.speaker: Chikwe Ihekweazu, WHO Africa acting regional director
a4217.name: Chikwe Ihekweazu
a4217.title: WHO Africa acting regional director
a4217.speech: Says that with strategic investment and governance, African nations can fund their health priorities effectively; speaking during a press briefing in Kigali, Rwanda ahead of AHAIC 2025, said there is need to map funding gaps and work closely with African governments to find sustainable solutions for areas that were being sponsored by USAID: “The focus must shift towards internally driven strategies while remaining open to strategic collaborations.” ; said this entails African governments prioritising internal revenue generation for healthcare, reducing out-of-pocket costs, and expanding universal healthcare coverage.

a4217.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer
a4217.name: Githinji Gitahi
a4217.title: Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer
a4217.speech: Urged African leaders and global stakeholders to rethink health investments to build resilient and sustainable health systems; said Africa’s economic and population growth challenges are deeply linked to healthcare financing: “Sub-Saharan Africa is facing an economic crisis, and the lack of fiscal space is a major issue” ; “Investing in health must be tied to population development, ensuring that every girl and woman have the right to make informed reproductive health choices.” ; called for investment shifts towards primary healthcare, warning that disproportionate funding for tertiary care leaves millions without access to essential services.

a4217.speaker: Githinji Gitahi, Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer (on USAID-funded programmes)
a4217.name: Githinji Gitahi
a4217.title: Amref Health Africa Group chief executive officer (on USAID-funded programmes)
a4217.speech: Said Amref had significant programmes worth about US$28 million in Kenya, Malawi, Zambia and Ethiopia that were being sponsored by USAID, the core of which was around maternal and child health and prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission: “So, as we speak, we are working with the governments to ensure that no child is going to be exposed to HIV because we are not protected during the mother’s pregnancy. That’s a risk. We had programmes on HIV prevention testing. For example, we had programmes on what you may call running care treatment centres for HIV, what we call the comprehensive care clinics that have stopped.” ; said Amref had health workers across Zambia, Malawi, Ethiopia and Kenya actively involved in care and treatment for prevention of mother-to-child HIV and tuberculosis who are now out of the health system though still trained.

a4217.speaker: Claudia Shilumani, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention director of external relations and strategic management
a4217.name: Claudia Shilumani
a4217.title: Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention director of external relations and strategic management
a4217.speech: Called for sustainable financing for African healthcare; said leaders across the continent should look at the need to explore alternative funding models, including public-private partnerships, to ensure long-term sustainability of health programmes and the continued progress made in improving public health.

a4243.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President (Direct Line broadcast)
a4243.name: Vladimir Putin
a4243.title: Russian President (Direct Line broadcast)
a4243.speech: Said on Direct Line that the head of the DPR, Pushilin, plans to visit Africa.

a4243.speaker: Russian Ambassador to Ghana
a4243.name: Russian Ambassador to Ghana
a4243.speech: Conveyed Putin's message to the new President of Ghana.

a4243.speaker: Prime Minister (cited in headline)
a4243.name: Prime Minister (cited in headline)
a4243.speech: “47 terrorist attacks have been stopped in Kenya in two years.”

a4243.speaker: Government of Somaliland
a4243.name: Government of Somaliland
a4243.speech: Has declared its readiness to host a US base.

a4243.speaker: Government of Chad
a4243.name: Government of Chad
a4243.speech: Demanded the completion of the withdrawal of French troops by January 31, 2025.

a4243.speaker: Government of Nigeria
a4243.name: Government of Nigeria
a4243.speech: Has rejected Niger's accusations of an attack on an oil pipeline.

a4243.speaker: Expert (unnamed)
a4243.name: Expert (unnamed)
a4243.speech: Told when Russian companies will be able to produce oil in Sudan.

a4243.speaker: Editor-in-chief of Pravda Niger (opinion)
a4243.name: Editor-in-chief of Pravda Niger (opinion)
a4243.speech: “Sanctions are like a reward. Why is Europe promoting the ‘African Initiative’?” – Opinion of the editor-in-chief.

a4243.speaker: African parliamentarians on a visit to Donbass
a4243.name: African parliamentarians on a visit to Donbass
a4243.speech: “The most important thing for us is to save lives.”

a4243.speaker: Professor at the University of Niamey
a4243.name: Professor at the University of Niamey

a4321.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a4321.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.speech: Expressed the wish to strengthen partnerships in maritime security and cybersecurity with the United States during his meeting with US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, saying the partnership would be from a regional and global perspective, “with a structured and predictable basis” ; “We maintain that the partnership for development and for cooperative security must go together. It is in the common interest.”

a4321.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a4321.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.speech: In his address, asked for the return of the Peace Corps to Cabo Verde to expand English-language teaching in the country, as a strategy for developing the potential of tourism, business and academic connectivity, “in a country open to the world and with a high level of economic freedom”.

a4321.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a4321.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.speech: Said the visit reinforces the excellent relations between Cabo Verde and the US and demonstrates an example of the “genuine” interest of the Biden administration in “win-win” partnerships with Africa: “Cabo Verde is an old and consistent partner of the US. We have a diaspora of thousands of Cape Verdean-American citizens proud of their origins” ; acknowledged US support in the fight against Covid-19, another Millennium Challenge Account package, the construction of the new embassy in Praia and the partnership programme with the New Hampshire National Guard ; “We want to strengthen our relations at the level of political and diplomatic dialogue, the attraction of investment and exports, training, science and technology.”

a4321.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a4321.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a4321.speech: Pointed out that, on the basis of history, the diaspora and the values of democracy, international law and multilateralism, Cabo Verde condemns Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the terrorist act by Hamas in Israel and the coups d’état that have occurred in Africa: “We have clearly and explicitly defined the US, Brazil, the European Union and the United Kingdom as strategic partners for cooperative security and defence.”

a4321.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde (official note)
a4321.name: Government of Cabo Verde (official note)
a4321.speech: According to a government note, this first visit by a US Secretary of State to Cabo Verde symbolises “the strong friendship and the exemplary partnership between the two countries”.

a4348.speaker: New annual report of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4348.name: New annual report of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4348.speech: Reports alarming and constantly deteriorating figures: 707,000 movements were recorded in Burkina Faso in 2023, the country ranking first in the world for long-term neglect of displacement, and the number of Burkinabe who lost their lives as a result of violence rose considerably, now exceeding the threshold of 8,000 victims ; states that "at least half a million people found themselves in an almost total blind spot in terms of aid" ; reveals a disastrous 70 per cent increase between 2022 and 2023 in the closure of health facilities, with nearly 400 establishments closed, leaving 3.6 million Burkinabe without access to care.

a4348.speaker: United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) figures
a4348.name: United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) figures
a4348.speech: According to UNHCR figures, the flow of refugees increased significantly, with a total of 148,317 people having crossed the borders.

a4388.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4388.title: African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.speech: Said Mozambique’s “real GDP growth is projected to increase to 2.7% in 2025 and 3.5% in 2026, pushed by a rebound in extractive sector activities” ; added “Inflation is projected to increase to 4.8% in 2025 and further increase to 5.2% in 2026 due to increased local food prices” ; notes that the forecasts follow a subdued GDP growth of 1.8% in 2024, “a significant decline from 5.4% growth in 2023, driven by declining output in extractive industries and agriculture”, and recalls that “inflation declined to 3.2% in 2024 from 7.0% in 2023, reflecting tight monetary policy and a stable exchange rate” ; “the fiscal deficit is projected to widen to 5.4% of GDP in 2025 and then narrow 4.5% in 2026 due to fiscal consolidation”.

a4388.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4388.title: African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.speech: Said the key downside risks to growth in Mozambique include “climate change, social unrest and its effects on economic activities, ODA cuts [cuts in Official Development Assistance/ foreign aid] and trade tensions” at a global level ; advises mitigation measures such as “improving spending efficiency, diversifying export markets with promotion of value-added industries to boost domestic consumption, and fostering dialogue among all political parties”.

a4388.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB), African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4388.title: African Economic Outlook 2025 report (Country Notes on Mozambique)
a4388.speech: Highlighted the low tax-to-GDP ratio, at around 23%, “falling below regional benchmarks, signaling unrealized fiscal potential” ; “Revenue mobilization is constrained by illicit financial flows, estimated at $1.3 billion annually, and by weak tax administration” ; noted the state’s “high wage bill, averaging 90% of tax revenue (2021–23) and rising debt service obligations significantly limit the fiscal space for development spending” ; concluded that “Exiting the Financial Action Task Force Grey List, tackling illicit financial flows, enforcing public-private partnership regulations will be essential to improving the investment climate and boosting economic resilience”.

a4407.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, president of the association Parcem
a4407.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a4407.title: president of the association Parcem
a4407.speech: “It is an immense market that plans to become a monetary union.” ; For Ndikumana, COMESA is a golden opportunity for Burundi, which can take advantage of its vast market of more than 400 million inhabitants; he explains that integration within COMESA could facilitate Burundian exports, create foreign direct investment and strengthen economic growth ; “All of this is a breath of fresh air in terms of foreign currency, while stimulating exports.”

a4407.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, president of the association Parcem
a4407.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a4407.title: president of the association Parcem
a4407.speech: Stresses the importance of infrastructure development within a transnational framework; according to him, Burundi must take advantage of the projects negotiated at a supranational level within these regional integration bodies ; “We have an infrastructure deficit.”

a4407.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, president of the association Parcem
a4407.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a4407.title: president of the association Parcem
a4407.speech: Emphasises the need to strengthen the business environment in Burundi ; “In order to benefit from this foreign direct investment, it is imperative to create a strategy to strengthen exports.” ; “Finding solutions to energy problems and strengthening good governance are crucial elements.”

a4407.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, president of the association Parcem
a4407.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a4407.title: president of the association Parcem
a4407.speech: Mentions the need to create a fund to support exporters; “the country must strengthen the capacity of businesses and exporters, as well as access to administrative information”; highlights the importance of reviving the production of promising companies, citing SOSUMO, which could export sugar within the sub-region ; “We must reactivate our industrial fabric of the past in order to produce quality exportable goods.”

a4407.speaker: Faustin Ndikumana, president of the association Parcem
a4407.name: Faustin Ndikumana
a4407.title: president of the association Parcem
a4407.speech: Recalls that Burundi must regularly pay its annual contribution to COMESA: “Burundi must not have arrears, as is sometimes the case in other organisations.”

a4407.speaker: Marie-Chantal Nijimbere, Burundian Minister of Trade
a4407.name: Marie-Chantal Nijimbere
a4407.title: Burundian Minister of Trade
a4407.speech: At a press conference on 23 October, underlined the importance of the summit as a “fine opportunity to do business and to meet people.”

a4407.speaker: Marie-Chantal Nijimbere, Burundian Minister of Trade
a4407.name: Marie-Chantal Nijimbere
a4407.title: Burundian Minister of Trade
a4407.speech: Highlighted certain initiatives financed by COMESA’s regional integration support mechanism, such as the economic adjustment facility intended to compensate for revenue losses caused by liberalisation reforms; also mentioned structural projects in Burundi, such as the ASCEDONIA programme of the Burundi Revenue Authority (OBR), the one-stop window supported by the African Development Bank (ADB) and the strengthening of the Burundi Bureau of Standards (BBN) ; welcomed the establishment of a simplified trade regime facilitating cross-border exchanges for small traders ; also underlined the importance of the Tripartite Free Trade Agreement between SADC, COMESA and the East African Community (EAC).

a4582.speaker: Thembisa, the leading model of HIV and TB in South Africa
a4582.name: Thembisa
a4582.title: the leading model of HIV and TB in South Africa
a4582.speech: According to Thembisa, just under 500,000 people aged 15 and older fell ill with TB in the country in 2005; by 2023, this number had dropped to around 330,000.

a4582.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4582.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a4582.speech: Still classifies South Africa as a high TB burden country, with an estimated 427 cases of TB per 100,000 people ; The WHO estimates that TB claimed 56,000 lives in the country last year.

a4582.speaker: Professor Thomas Scriba, TB expert from the University of Cape Town
a4582.name: Professor Thomas Scriba
a4582.title: TB expert from the University of Cape Town
a4582.speech: "Earlier identification of people in early stages of TB disease is really critical if we hope to control TB." He said: "Better for public health because treatment would stop transmission of the TB bacterium at an earlier stage of disease when the patient may be less infectious. This would also reduce the period of infectiousness of the patient, thus protecting those in contact with the patient."

a4582.speaker: Professor Thomas Scriba, TB expert from the University of Cape Town
a4582.name: Professor Thomas Scriba
a4582.title: TB expert from the University of Cape Town
a4582.speech: "There is a lot of ongoing research to advance blood biomarkers for early TB... Unfortunately, they are not yet ready for prime time."

a4582.speaker: Research on blood markers (much of it conducted in South Africa)
a4582.name: Research on blood markers (much of it conducted in South Africa)
a4582.speech: Has shown that by looking at certain blood markers, it is possible to predict with a high degree of accuracy whether someone will develop TB symptoms in the next six months.

a4582.speaker: Landmark study presented at a major scientific conference in early 2021
a4582.name: Landmark study presented at a major scientific conference in early 2021
a4582.speech: Confirmed that targeted universal testing (TUT) increases TB detection.

a4582.speaker: TUT study
a4582.name: TUT study
a4582.speech: In one TUT study, it was found that more than half of around 30,000 people who tested positive for TB did not have TB symptoms.

a4582.speaker: Recent research
a4582.name: Recent research
a4582.speech: Suggests working-age men are particularly worth targeting even if they are not living with HIV.

a4582.speaker: Dr Norbert Ndjeka, top TB official in the National Department of Health
a4582.name: Dr Norbert Ndjeka
a4582.title: top TB official in the National Department of Health
a4582.speech: Has been vocal in his support of TUT; earlier this year, he told Spotlight that TUT is national policy and that it has been rolled out across the country since 2022.

a4582.speaker: Dr Norbert Ndjeka, top TB official in the National Department of Health
a4582.name: Dr Norbert Ndjeka
a4582.title: top TB official in the National Department of Health
a4582.speech: Explains that TB programmes are primarily funded by the state; says the state will step in should the Global Fund pull out; says provinces are starting to procure their own X-ray machines, most of which are currently paid for by donors such as the Global Fund and USAID.

a4582.speaker: South Africa's National Department of Health (figures shared by the department)
a4582.name: South Africa's National Department of Health (figures shared by the department)
a4582.speech: Figures shared by the department suggest around 2.1 million people were tested for pulmonary TB in 2019; this dropped below 2 million in 2020 and 2021 due to the Covid-19 pandemic, then increased to 2.4 million in 2022 and 2.7 million in 2023.

a4673.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.name: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni
a4673.title: Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.speech: “There won't be mayhem. There won't be a repeat of the July 2021 unrest in this country when our law enforcement agencies are at work”; vowed that the country's law enforcement agencies will crack down on individuals who threaten to disrupt the upcoming 29 May general elections.

a4673.speaker: Bonginkosi Khanyile, interim youth leader (Gauteng Youth Leader) of the Umkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP)
a4673.name: Bonginkosi Khanyile
a4673.title: interim youth leader (Gauteng Youth Leader) of the Umkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP)
a4673.speech: Commenting on the legal battle with the ANC over the trademark and registration of MKP, said on Wednesday during a press briefing in Johannesburg that they were willing to lay down their lives if Zuma and the MKP are not allowed to take part in the elections; reiterated his stance that there will be violence if the MK Party is removed from the ballot.

a4673.speaker: Ntebo Mokobo (@MokoboNtebo), SABC News journalist (social media post)
a4673.name: Ntebo Mokobo (@MokoboNtebo)
a4673.title: SABC News journalist (social media post)
a4673.speech: “The MK Party Gauteng Youth Leader Bonginkosi Khanyile has reiterated his stance that there will be violence if the MK Party is removed from the ballot #sabcnews” (March 13, 2024).

a4673.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.name: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni
a4673.title: Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.speech: Briefing the media in Tshwane on Thursday on the outcomes of the Cabinet meeting, echoed President Cyril Ramaphosa's sentiments that the country's law enforcement agencies should arrest individuals who threaten violence ahead of the elections; said Cabinet did not discuss threats of violence ahead of the elections but reassured South Africans that law enforcement agencies would not be caught off guard as in 2021: “Anybody who threatens violence when we have dispute resolution mechanisms for either elections or any type of dispute, does not deserve to live among South Africans, and law enforcement officers and agencies must make sure they're brought to book.”

a4673.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a4673.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4673.title: President of South Africa
a4673.speech: Sentiments that the country's law enforcement agencies should arrest individuals who threaten violence ahead of the elections.

a4673.speaker: Umkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP)
a4673.name: Umkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP)
a4673.speech: Has distanced itself from the threats of violence made by its members.

a4673.speaker: Electoral Commission of SA (IEC)
a4673.name: Electoral Commission of SA (IEC)
a4673.speech: Confirmed it is investigating the issue; condemned the threats of violence and anarchy by the party and called on all parties to abide by the Electoral Code of Conduct.

a4673.speaker: Democratic Alliance (DA) (letter to US Secretary of State Antony Blinken)
a4673.name: Democratic Alliance (DA) (letter to US Secretary of State Antony Blinken)
a4673.speech: Called on Washington to send an election observer mission to South Africa for the polls in May, raising concerns of election interference and possible vote rigging by the governing ANC.

a4673.speaker: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.name: Khumbudzo Ntshavheni
a4673.title: Minister in the Presidency of South Africa
a4673.speech: On the DA letter to the US: criticised the DA, saying that the party was undermining South Africa's sovereignty by approaching the US; said South Africa had always held free and fair elections since the dawn of democracy, adding that the US was the last country to send observers as it faces criticism of voter suppression in certain states; said South Africa would not allow a country such as the US to observe the upcoming polls and “play big brother” ; “South Africa is a sovereign republic, and we have our own rules and own observer mechanisms, and this democracy has stood the test of time. And it has stood the test of time because we have the Electoral Commission that has time and again shown its independence, resilience and astuteness. We have been leading, not only the continent, but the world in making sure that we deliver free and fair elections. And there has not been intimidation and the violation of people's right to vote.” ; took a swipe at the DA, suggesting that it wanted to be a “puppet of another country” that wants to diminish the sovereignty of South Africa.

a4673.speaker: US Embassy in Tshwane
a4673.name: US Embassy in Tshwane
a4673.speech: Said this week that the country recognised South Africa's sovereignty and did not believe the IEC was incapable of conducting free and fair elections.

a4742.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4742.name: Donald Trump
a4742.title: US President
a4742.speech: Said he would cut off all future funding to South Africa due to poor treatment of “certain classes of people”; according to him, South Africa is seizing land and mistreating some of its citizens without concerns about the violations of their rights ; “The United States won’t stand for it” ; “South Africa is confiscating land and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY. It is a bad situation that the Radical Left Media doesn’t want to so much as mention. A massive Human Rights VIOLATION, at a minimum, is happening for all to see.”

a4742.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President (post on X)
a4742.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4742.title: South African President (post on X)
a4742.speech: Says his government’s land policy is in the interest of citizens and does not warrant official criticism from the US ; insisted that the expropriation act was constitutional and said that the act is a legal process that allows equitable access to land and addresses historical disparities ; “South Africa is a constitutional democracy deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice, and equality. The recently adopted Expropriation Act is not a confiscation instrument, but a constitutionally mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner as guided by the constitution” ; said South Africa adopted the laws to balance land use and protect property rights as obtainable in the United States of America and other countries, the goal being to protect “the need for public usage of land and the protection of rights of property owners.”

a4742.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President (post on X)
a4742.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4742.title: South African President (post on X)
a4742.speech: Noted that the country is looking forward to engaging with the Trump administration over its land reform policy and issues of bilateral interest: “We are certain that out of those engagements, we will share a better and common understanding over these matters.”

a4742.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President (post on X)
a4742.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a4742.title: South African President (post on X)
a4742.speech: Stated that external aid from the US is significantly less than the country’s domestic funding: “With the exception of PEPFAR Aid, which constitutes 17 per cent of South Africa’s HIV/Aids programme, there is no other significant funding that is provided by the United States in South Africa”; noted that rather, the US is a key strategic political and trade partner for South Africa.

a4827.speaker: Communique of the Nigerien Council of Ministers
a4827.name: Communique of the Nigerien Council of Ministers
a4827.speech: states that "Since 2013 the State has been implementing a Strategy for the Sustainable Development of Livestock Farming (SDDEL 2013-2035) with the aim of increasing animal production, notably through several Programmes for the Improvement of Local Cattle Production", and explains that "these programmes are intended to meet national consumption needs for milk and meat and to increase producers' incomes" ; stresses that "it appeared necessary to take measures to prevent risks at the various stages of production, importation, distribution and export of the materials used" ; specifies that "the purpose of this draft ordinance is therefore to secure, moralise and organise the use of animal production material"

a4827.speaker: Nigerien Government (Council of Ministers communique)
a4827.name: Nigerien Government (Council of Ministers communique)
a4827.speech: reports, on the decree creating the National Centre for the Improvement of Animal Production, that "Niger, despite its large herd, continues to resort to imports of milk and dairy products to meet the needs of the population. This situation results from shortcomings in the institutional framework and in production techniques" ; maintains that "within the framework of developing a genuine policy of improving local breeds, the creation of a specific service is proving necessary" and that the decree "aims, through an appropriate technique, at an increase in the milk and meat production performance of our local breeds" ; "It will also allow growth in the national economy through an increase in animal production"

a4839.speaker: Stakeholders at the dialogue on domestic financing for HIV and TB, Abuja
a4839.name: Stakeholders at the dialogue on domestic financing for HIV and TB
a4839.title: Abuja
a4839.speech: renewed calls for multi-sectoral collaboration and sustainable domestic financing to sustain Nigeria's response to HIV and Tuberculosis (TB), amid dwindling foreign aid; say financing remains insufficient to meet national needs despite recent steps such as the N4.8bn budgeted for HIV treatment and the establishment of an AIDS Trust Fund.

a4839.speaker: Amobi Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (represented by his deputy, Abubakar Zango)
a4839.name: Amobi Ogah
a4839.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (represented by his deputy, Abubakar Zango)
a4839.speech: said Nigeria requires an estimated $8bn annually to sustain its HIV/AIDS response and emphasised that Nigeria must take ownership of its health response rather than depend solely on external donors: "But in the face of recent changes in the global funding landscape, occasioned by the suspension of funding for African health systems by the US government, further gaps in funding will negatively impact the country's fight against HIV/AIDS and TB" ; "It is my opinion that the suspension of funding of Africa's health systems by the US government is a blessing in disguise because I believe that the Nigerian government must take the lead in funding the response to public health threats such as HIV, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, and not rely solely on foreign interventions."

a4839.speaker: Amobi Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (represented by his deputy, Abubakar Zango)
a4839.name: Amobi Ogah
a4839.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (represented by his deputy, Abubakar Zango)
a4839.speech: explained that since the withdrawal of funding, Nigerians in both the public and private spaces have begun conversations on how to rejig their financing architecture: "So far, many brilliant and innovative solutions on how to mobilise domestic funding for the response against HIV and TB in Nigeria have been rolled out. But there is a need to streamline some of these solutions and, if need be, provide a legislative framework for their implementation" ; further called for multi-sectoral collaboration and stronger partnerships among civil society organisations, government, and the private sector to ensure cost-efficient and sustainable interventions.

a4839.speaker: Abdulkadir Ibrahim, National Coordinator of NEPWHAN (Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Nigeria)
a4839.name: Abdulkadir Ibrahim
a4839.title: National Coordinator of NEPWHAN (Network of People Living with HIV/AIDS in Nigeria)
a4839.speech: emphasised the urgency of strengthening domestic health financing, especially for HIV, due to uncertainties in global health funding and shifts in US government policy; stated that about 80-85 per cent of HIV funding in Nigeria comes from foreign aid, while the Nigerian government contributes only about 15 per cent; stressed the need to look inward for sustainable financing through health insurance schemes, local philanthropy, and domestic resource mobilisation: "We are looking into issues around health insurance, how our people will be registered into a health insurance scheme, which will be more sustainable and affordable if people have to pay" ; "The drugs that people are currently getting for free are being paid for by someone - it is taxpayers' money, either from the US or from contributions by other countries."

a4839.speaker: Abdul-Rahman Momodu, Chairman of NEPWHAN's Board of Trustees
a4839.name: Abdul-Rahman Momodu
a4839.title: Chairman of NEPWHAN's Board of Trustees
a4839.speech: emphasised commitment and leadership in the fight against HIV, and noted that HIV is not just a health issue but also a social one that must be openly addressed.

a4860.speaker: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a4860.name: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a4860.speech: Stressed the "danger of the continuing escalation in the West Bank and of the violations of the holy sites in Jerusalem" and reaffirmed his country's rejection of "any attempts to displace Palestinians in the West Bank and in the Gaza Strip."

a4860.speaker: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a4860.name: King Abdullah II of Jordan
a4860.speech: Also called for "restoring the ceasefire in the Gaza Strip and immediately resuming the delivery of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip."

a4860.speaker: Royal Hashemite Court (two statements)
a4860.name: Royal Hashemite Court (two statements)
a4860.speech: Stated that the meetings, held on Tuesday at the Al Husseiniya Palace in Amman, discussed regional developments and efforts to end the Israeli war of annihilation in the Gaza Strip; and that the US delegation included congressional aides as well as members of the Senate and the House of Representatives, while the French delegation included senators and representatives of the French-Jordanian Friendship Group and of the Group for Contact, Reflection, Monitoring and Solidarity with Eastern Christians, Minorities in the Middle East and Kurds.

a4870.speaker: Creative Associates International, Inc. / Creative Procurement Department (tender notice)
a4870.name: Creative Associates International
a4870.title: Inc. / Creative Procurement Department (tender notice)
a4870.speech: Issued Request for Quotation No. 019 for staff health insurance, published 8/11/2024 with a bid deadline of 24/11/2024, on behalf of the Inclusive Governance for Resilience (IGR) project, funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Contract No. 72068521CA00004, stating that all correspondence and questions concerning this RFQ must reference the above solicitation number and be submitted only by email; "Creative encourages bidders to express their interest in this contract by submitting an offer in accordance with the instructions contained in the call for tenders. Creative will award the contract to the bidders who submit the best offer."

a4870.speaker: Creative Associates International, Inc. (tender notice)
a4870.name: Creative Associates International
a4870.title: Inc. (tender notice)
a4870.speech: Stated that Creative Associates International is implementing the five-year USAID-funded Inclusive Governance for Resilience (IGR) project in Burkina Faso, that the programme aims to shift the governance paradigm from a supply-and-demand model to one of shared responsibility and shared success, and that the IGR project works in 26 communes in partnership with local organisations in the Sahel, Centre Nord, Est, Nord, Cascades, Hauts-Bassins, Centre Ouest and Centre Sud regions; and that Creative is seeking an insurance company to provide health coverage for its staff from 1 January to 31 December 2025, covering at least 150 people including at least 80 children.

a4870.speaker: Creative Associates International, Inc. (reservations clause)
a4870.name: Creative Associates International
a4870.title: Inc. (reservations clause)
a4870.speech: "Creative reserves the right not to act on all or part of this call for tenders, or not to select any insurance company." ; Stated that Creative reserves the right to visit a potential bidder's place of business to verify that it is a legal commercial entity and possesses the organisational and management skills required to assume the required responsibilities, and that bidders who do not comply with the instructions of this RFQ may be excluded from selection.

a4870.speaker: US federal acquisition provisions 52.204-24 and 52.204-26 / John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232), Section 889 (regulatory text)
a4870.name: US federal acquisition provisions 52.204-24 and 52.204-26 / John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019 (Pub. L. 115-232)
a4870.title: Section 889 (regulatory text)
a4870.speech: Prohibits the head of an executive agency, as of 13 August 2019, from procuring or obtaining, or extending or renewing a contract to procure or obtain, any equipment, system or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system, or as critical technology as part of any system; and, as of 13 August 2020, from entering into, extending or renewing a contract with an entity that uses any such equipment, system or service, whether or not that use is in performance of a federal contract; and requires the vendor to review the excluded parties list in the System for Award Management (SAM) and to make the corresponding representations and disclosures.

a5085.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (statement to APA)
a5085.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (statement to APA)
a5085.speech: According to a statement to APA on Friday, the MCC has selected Liberia as newly eligible to develop a compact, in recognition of the country's commitment to pursuing critical economic and democratic governance reforms; MCC expects all partner countries to continue to demonstrate an ongoing commitment to the principles of inclusive democratic governance that underpin MCC's eligibility criteria; the statement said the size and content of the final program is contingent on analytical work done in partnership between MCC and the government of Liberia, the availability of funds, and approval of the proposed program by the MCC Board of Directors.

a5085.speaker: MCC and the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia (statement)
a5085.name: MCC and the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia (statement)
a5085.speech: Said it is looking forward to working closely with the Liberian government to launch the compact development process.

a5085.speaker: Alice Albright, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a5085.name: Alice Albright
a5085.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a5085.speech: "MCC is proud of our longstanding history with Liberia and is enthusiastic about embarking a new partnership to advance opportunities for the people of Liberia."

a5104.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a5104.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC)
a5104.speech: Became the latest voice to demand that President Lazarus Chakwera bow out gracefully after the September 16 General Election; the church grouping says the responsible path for Chakwera is to publicly concede and call for calm among his supporters.

a5104.speaker: Reverend Billy Gamah, MCC chairperson
a5104.name: Reverend Billy Gamah
a5104.title: MCC chairperson
a5104.speech: Minced no words in declaring that, based on the partial presidential results announced by the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) last night, “the table cannot change to deliver victory” for Chakwera ; “A public statement by the President acknowledging defeat would not only be an act of statesmanship but also a powerful gesture to encourage his supporters to accept the outcome peacefully” ; “We believe that conceding early, even before the official announcement, will show maturity, promote peace, and help the nation move forward without violence or unnecessary tension.”

a5104.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former president of Malawi
a5104.name: Bakili Muluzi
a5104.title: former president of Malawi
a5104.speech: Confirmed that he had personally urged Chakwera to concede and call Mutharika to congratulate him. Muluzi argued that doing so would defuse political tensions and safeguard Malawi’s democratic stability, reminding Chakwera that “there is life after State House.”

a5137.speaker: Richard Asiedu, Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.name: Richard Asiedu
a5137.title: Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.speech: Disclosed to GBC in Kumasi that the Ashanti regional office saved more than 52 thousand Ghana Cedis in over and wrongful billing from utility service providers to consumers from January to March this year, following more than 300 formal complaints, and noted that the office was able to resolve about 90 percent of the complaints: “Most of them are billing-related issues, be it water or electricity. We've been able to help consumers in the regions save about GHC 52,000. The utility service providers can also report consumers, especially the state-owned institutions, when they're also owing. For the 1st quarter, we've collected GHC 4,500 for them.”

a5137.speaker: Richard Asiedu, Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.name: Richard Asiedu
a5137.title: Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.speech: Noted that the 'Market Invasion' initiative also allows staff of the Commission to distribute educational materials to augment the verbal interaction with sellers and buyers, centring on the processes they need to go through in seeking redress for their grievances with services received from the utility providers; urged utility consumers to repose trust and confidence in the PURC with their grievances for a peaceful and satisfactory solution.

a5137.speaker: Richard Asiedu, Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.name: Richard Asiedu
a5137.title: Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC)
a5137.speech: On the rift between the ECG, the Kumasi Technical University, and the Ashanti Regional Minister, for which the Ashanti East Regional Manager of the ECG was arrested for disconnecting the University over its indebtedness, the PRO said none of the feuding parties has made any formal complaint to the Office for intervention.

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.speech: Told journalists at a press briefing in Accra that the government had constituted a team to engage the MCC to secure the future of the compact: "this engagement is about the possible next steps after the inquiry and channels for sharing information as part of this enquiry"; according to him, the team would visit the United States, possibly next week, as part of its engagement.

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana (statement)
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana (statement)
a5288.speech: A statement issued by Mr Nkrumah last Tuesday announced the suspension of the concession agreement and explained that the decision followed the "detection of fundamental and material breaches of PDS's obligation in the provision of Payment Securities (Demand Guarantees) for the transaction which were discovered upon further due diligence"; "The demand guarantees were key prerequisites for the lease of assets on 1st March, 2019 to secure the assets that were transferred to the concessionaire," it said; following from that, the re-transfer of ECG assets had begun, while investigations continued, both at home and abroad, the statement said.

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.speech: Said a full-scale enquiry into the detected breaches had commenced and was expected to be completed within 30 days, and that the team conducting the enquiry comprised insurance investigation experts, officials of the Energy and Finance ministries and officials of the ECG and the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA): "The enquiry will determine the nature of the breaches and advise on suggested next steps. By Tuesday, the team is expected in Doha, Qatar as part of the enquiry. All interested parties are cooperating with the enquiry at this stage."

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.speech: Explained that final efforts to ensure a smooth transition between ECG and PDS officials were proceeding without any incidents: "We reiterate the fact that this breach was discovered by the due diligence of the Ghanaian authorities through the ECG and with the support of state agencies"; he stressed that "for the avoidance of doubt, the provision of the payment guarantee has always been a condition precedent and was never changed to a condition subsequent, as is being speculated by some persons."

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.speech: Said initial due diligence led by the transaction advisors did not detect anything wrong, but second level checks led by the Ghana side initially yielded a response from Al-Koot confirming the guarantee, and a third level check resulted in the detection of anomalies within Al-Koot, triggering a fourth level check: "The fourth level check involved sending an initial team from the Ghana Mission in Qatar to engage with Al-Koot officials for further verification. This fourth level check further proved the anomalies and suggested untoward action which is now the subject of the full-scale inquiry."

a5288.speaker: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.name: Kojo Oppong Nkrumah
a5288.title: Minister of Information of Ghana
a5288.speech: Urged the African Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP), the Institute of Energy Security (IES) and other persons who had raised issues to patiently wait for the outcome of the investigations; asked if PDS had injected $580 million into its operations, he declined to answer, on grounds that all concerns would be addressed after investigations had been completed.

a5288.speaker: John Peter Amewu, Minister of Energy of Ghana
a5288.name: John Peter Amewu
a5288.title: Minister of Energy of Ghana
a5288.speech: Said due diligence was ongoing to unravel all issues surrounding the matter, and assured the public that there would be uninterrupted supply of power, in spite of the issues surrounding the deal.

a5288.speaker: Minority Caucus in Parliament (Ghana)
a5288.name: Minority Caucus in Parliament (Ghana)
a5288.speech: Has called for the immediate termination of the PDS Concession Agreement to ensure efficient and sustainable delivery of power; it also called for the prosecution of all those responsible for the fraudulent guarantee, as confirmed by the Minister of Energy, and to ensure full refund of all money appropriated by PDS and their collaborators through the alleged fraudulent schemes; the Minority served notice that it would not countenance any attempt by the government to reintroduce other so-called private sector players or the constitution of a special purpose vehicle (SPV); it said it was their expectation that in the coming weeks the MCC of the United States would apprise itself of the facts and take appropriate actions to preserve the image of MiDA, and warned that other legitimate options to delve into the scandal were beckoning and it would actively take advantage of them if the government refused to heed its patriotic call.

a5288.speaker: John Abdulai Jinapor, NDC Member of Parliament for Yapei Kusawgu and former Deputy Minister of Energy
a5288.name: John Abdulai Jinapor
a5288.title: NDC Member of Parliament for Yapei Kusawgu and former Deputy Minister of Energy
a5288.speech: Called on the government to, as a matter of urgency, dissolve the current ECG Board and appoint a competent, non-partisan board and restructure the current management of the ECG to ensure that they sign performance bonds with the board for efficient supply of power to Ghanaians; he alleged that the so-called suspension of the concession was only a smokescreen to cover up the government's supposed "complicity in the whole scandal of gargantuan proportion" and therefore must be terminated without further delay: "As it stands, the concession in its current state will certainly not serve the interest of Ghana. The concession is highly inimical to the aspirations of Ghana's power sector goals and can tip our dear country into 'Dumsor' because of choking debts, not because independent power producers (IPPs) lack capacity to produce power"; according to him, the concession, if left to continue, had the potential of destabilising the whole energy sector, with very serious consequences, including rising cost of power and crippling power generation companies.

a5288.speaker: John Abdulai Jinapor, NDC Member of Parliament for Yapei Kusawgu and former Deputy Minister of Energy
a5288.name: John Abdulai Jinapor
a5288.title: NDC Member of Parliament for Yapei Kusawgu and former Deputy Minister of Energy
a5288.speech: Said that as a result of a deliberate mismanagement of yet another project by former President Mahama, IPPs, for the first time in the history of the country, recently served a seven-day ultimatum to the government to release funds to pay all outstanding debts or they shut down, and said the debts were estimated at $300 million as of June 2019; he recalled that the Minority cautioned the government against the deal on the floor of Parliament when it was discovered that the Ghanaian shareholders in the transaction had questionable records, and alleged that at the time of filing the documents some of the partners to the consortium (TG Energy Solutions) had neither offices nor physical location per the documents presented to the Mines and Energy Committee of Parliament by MiDA.

a5316.speaker: Peter Amo Bediako, Director of Takoradi Port
a5316.name: Peter Amo Bediako
a5316.title: Director of Takoradi Port
a5316.speech: Has stated that the Port's achievement in the year 2024 is a testament to the resilience, dedication, and innovation that continue to drive its operations.

a5316.speaker: Peter Amo Bediako, Director of Takoradi Port
