a5316.name: Peter Amo Bediako
a5316.title: Director of Takoradi Port
a5316.speech: Speaking to journalists at a press soiree, announced that as of November 2024 the Port had recorded an impressive 32.28% growth in cargo volume, rising from 7.1 million metric tonnes in November 2023 to 9.4 million metric tonnes, and that cruise or passenger ship calls recorded a 100% growth, increasing from seven cruise vessel calls at the end of November 2023 to 14 at the end of November 2024; he indicated these achievements reflected the Port's unwavering commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction, and most importantly the positive brand image generated by the professional coverage and reportage by the media. He gave a breakdown showing imported cargo volume of 2,877,273 metric tonnes (up 11.03%), exported cargo volume of 6,472,998 metric tonnes (up 44%), and transit cargo volume of 51,086 metric tonnes (up 2,173.52%).

a5316.speaker: Peter Amo Bediako, Director of Takoradi Port
a5316.name: Peter Amo Bediako
a5316.title: Director of Takoradi Port
a5316.speech: Noted that the 11% decline in Container TEU traffic in 2024, to 28,257 TEUs as at end of November compared to 31,763 TEUs in the same period in 2023, could be attributed largely to the delay in start of commercial operation of the YILPORT-ATSL Container Terminal.

a5624.speaker: Delegation of the European Union to Tanzania (statement)
a5624.name: Delegation of the European Union to Tanzania (statement)
a5624.speech: Said the agreement also focuses on looking after the new arrivals who are temporarily hosted at the transit centre in Kigoma Region.

a5624.speaker: Christine Grau, EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.name: Christine Grau
a5624.title: EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.speech: Said in a statement that the global increase in crises has led to an unprecedented number of refugees in urgent need of support around the world ; "That is why today I am proud to announce the signing of a 9.2 bn/- contract with UNHCR here in Tanzania. This crucial agreement will directly benefit refugees in Tanzania, ensuring their protection, enabling them to lead dignified lives and supporting their access to livelihoods."

a5624.speaker: Christine Grau, EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.name: Christine Grau
a5624.title: EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.speech: Added that the EU remains firmly committed to humanitarian values and international solidarity: "We must continue working together to address these global challenges and uphold the rights and dignity of every individual seeking refuge."

a5624.speaker: Christine Grau, EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.name: Christine Grau
a5624.title: EU Ambassador to Tanzania and the East African Community
a5624.speech: Said from January to June this year, over 3,000 refugees were received in Kigoma ; "UNHCR and partners continue to provide services to 85,105 Congolese refugees residing at Nyarugusu Camp. These individuals are provided with immediate life-saving assistance, including safe shelter, food, health services, clean water and sanitation facilities and other essential support." ; said that given the dire circumstances under which many refugees flee, often with only clothes on their backs and a few belongings, access to health, shelter, clean water, hygiene and sanitation facilities is critical ; "These services not only reduce mortality and morbidity but also uphold the dignity, protection and overall well-being of asylum seekers and refugees."

a5624.speaker: Zulqarnain Hussain Anjum, UNHCR Representative in Tanzania
a5624.name: Zulqarnain Hussain Anjum
a5624.title: UNHCR Representative in Tanzania
a5624.speech: "Standing with Congolese refugees and asylum seekers in Tanzania is not just our responsibility, it is a reflection of our shared humanity."

a5675.speaker: Safiullah Noorzai, who works with Aseel, a humanitarian tech platform
a5675.name: Safiullah Noorzai
a5675.title: who works with Aseel, a humanitarian tech platform
a5675.speech: Said the aftershock caused panic and halted rescue efforts as it sent rocks sliding down mountains, cutting off roads further and making it dangerous to dig through rubble; said more people had been injured, likely pushing the death toll higher.

a5675.speaker: Residents
a5675.name: Residents
a5675.speech: According to residents, some partially damaged homes were destroyed by the second earthquake.

a5675.speaker: Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban administration spokesperson
a5675.name: Zabihullah Mujahid
a5675.title: Taliban administration spokesperson
a5675.speech: Said at least 1,411 people are known to have died so far, 3,124 have been injured and more than 5,400 houses destroyed.

a5675.speaker: UN coordinator in Afghanistan
a5675.name: UN coordinator in Afghanistan
a5675.speech: Said the death toll was sure to rise further.

a5675.speaker: Save the Children (aid group)
a5675.name: Save the Children (aid group)
a5675.speech: Called on the international community to urgently release emergency funds; said the earthquake has disrupted sources of clean water, raising fears of disease, and restricted access to food.

a5675.speaker: Samira Sayed Rahman, Programs and Advocacy Director at Save the Children
a5675.name: Samira Sayed Rahman
a5675.title: Programs and Advocacy Director at Save the Children
a5675.speech: “This is now a race against time to save lives – to get injured people out of remote villages cut off by massive rock falls and to get clean water, food, and shelter in.”

a5675.speaker: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF)
a5675.name: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF)
a5675.speech: Warned on Tuesday that thousands of children were at risk; said it was sending medicines, warm clothing, tents and tarpaulins for shelter, and hygiene items such as soap, detergent, towels, sanitary pads, and water buckets.

a5675.speaker: World Health Organization
a5675.name: World Health Organization
a5675.speech: “Damaged roads, ongoing aftershocks, and remote locations of many villages severely impede the delivery of aid”, adding that over 12,000 people had been affected by the quake ; “The pre-earthquake fragility of the health system means local capacity is overwhelmed, creating total dependence on external actors.”

a5675.speaker: Safiullah Noorzai, Aseel
a5675.name: Safiullah Noorzai
a5675.title: Aseel
a5675.speech: Said food and tents were desperately needed, adding that with their houses in ruins, many people were living in the open amid a fear of aftershocks.

a5675.speaker: Diplomats and aid officials
a5675.name: Diplomats and aid officials
a5675.speech: According to diplomats and aid officials, crises elsewhere in the world, along with donor frustration over the Taliban’s policies toward women and curbs on aid workers, have been a factor in funding cuts.

a5690.speaker: Joint Committee on Investment and Concessions and Transport of the House of Representatives (Liberia)
a5690.name: Joint Committee on Investment and Concessions and Transport of the House of Representatives (Liberia)
a5690.speech: Last week ordered the suspension of all Liberia Traffic Management (LTM) operations, for failure to appear before lawmakers for an investigative hearing that was scheduled for Thursday, July 31, 2025, effectively returning complete operational control to the Ministry of Transport.

a5690.speaker: Commercial drivers / protesters
a5690.name: Commercial drivers / protesters
a5690.speech: Staged a mass protest against what they described as inhumane treatment under the new agreement; the protesters decried excessive ticketing and alleged extortion by LTM officers, claiming the company is exploiting drivers under the guise of traffic enforcement.

a5690.speaker: Plenary of the Liberian Senate
a5690.name: Plenary of the Liberian Senate
a5690.speech: On Thursday, July 24, 2025, mandated its leadership to request that President Joseph Nyuma Boakai immediately halt the implementation of the Liberia Traffic Management Incorporated (LTM-I) concession agreement until further consultations and clarity provided.

a5690.speaker: Employees of the Ministry of Transport
a5690.name: Employees of the Ministry of Transport
a5690.speech: Staged a series of protests calling attention to the fate waiting them, if the Liberia Traffic Management were to take full control of license production and issuance to the public.

a5760.speaker: Moses Maunganidze, GMAZ secretary
a5760.name: Moses Maunganidze
a5760.title: GMAZ secretary
a5760.speech: Announced that GMAZ members have already purchased over 35,000 tonnes of wheat from ARDA during the ongoing marketing season: “This wheat buying shows our continued support for local farmers and national food security” ; “We are committed to reducing imports and strengthening local grain supply chains” ; said the association would continue to procure more wheat during the remaining six to eight weeks of the marketing season: “Our members are still active on the market, and we expect to increase our wheat intake significantly before the end of the season.”

a5760.speaker: Moses Maunganidze, GMAZ secretary
a5760.name: Moses Maunganidze
a5760.title: GMAZ secretary
a5760.speech: Said that due to global supply challenges and rising input costs GMAZ remained determined to prioritise local sourcing: “It is important to build resilience within our own systems. That is why we are investing in partnerships that support domestic production and protect our economy from external shocks” ; revealed that structured agreements like the one signed with ARDA form part of GMAZ’s long-term strategy: “This deal is not just about maize. It’s about building a reliable, farmer-focused value chain that supports productivity, guarantees supply, and creates sustainable business opportunities across the agriculture sector.”

a5760.speaker: Shingirai Jenah, ARDA operations director
a5760.name: Shingirai Jenah
a5760.title: ARDA operations director
a5760.speech: Hailed the agreement as a milestone that bridges the long standing gap between primary producers and the commercial market: “This partnership is a big step in linking farmers with buyers” ; “It will boost local production and reduce our dependence on imports, which have been draining our much needed and scarce foreign currency” ; added that the agreement also supports smallholder farmers, promotes structured markets, and helps align private sector and government efforts: “Together with GMAZ, we are creating a national model that supports localised value chains, enhances food security, and ensures the participation of women, youth, and vulnerable communities in agriculture.”

a5832.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5832.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5832.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5832.speech: Has emphasized an urgent need to reprogram and redirect certain projects that are not yielding the desired returns, particularly in light of the recent reduction in USAID aid: "We are facing a significant shock due to the USAID aid cut, and immediate measures are being taken to mitigate its impact." ; reiterated that discussions will soon be held with partners to reallocate resources to critical sectors impacted by the aid reduction ; acknowledges the situation, noting that hard conversations are underway across the government to address the ongoing challenges: "Many Liberians have lost their jobs, interventions to vital sectors have been reduced, and it is essential for us to implement critical measures." ; reveals that government, alongside its partners, will convene a roundtable in April to address emerging challenges and explore solutions that ensure the uninterrupted implementation of the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development. He reassures Liberians that the government remains committed to delivering on its agenda.

a5832.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5832.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a5832.title: Liberian Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a5832.speech: Describes the launch of the GREAT Project as a "significant opportunity" for Liberia's continued progress. He explains that the Project would focus on expanding digital public services, increasing tax revenues, strengthening accountability and transparency, and enhancing capacity building and implementation support.

a5832.speaker: Oyewole Afuye, Acting World Bank Country Manager
a5832.name: Oyewole Afuye
a5832.title: Acting World Bank Country Manager
a5832.speech: Congratulates the Government of Liberia for the successful launch of the Project which is expected to "leverage digital solutions and deepen institutional reforms to modernize the public administration and improve government efficiency, ultimately benefitting all Liberians." He notes that the six years Project will support the government's ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development in achieving great transparency, accountability, and efficiency. Specifically, he outlines that it will address three key challenges - a weak system for delivering administrative services due to low state presence and infrastructure constraints across the country, a strained fiscal outlook due to low domestic resource mobilization and limited accountability for managing public resources with uneven service delivery results. The World Bank Acting Country Manager calls on all ministries, agencies and commissions and development partners to support the delivery of the project and help to sustain policy dialogue on the reforms.

a5975.speaker: Herry Sudradjat, Ambassador of Indonesia to Mozambique
a5975.name: Herry Sudradjat
a5975.title: Ambassador of Indonesia to Mozambique
a5975.speech: Said on the occasion that the donation of school desks by EMP-Buzi Hydrocarbons was a way to strengthen the partnership between the governments of Indonesia and Mozambique in the field of development cooperation ; according to Ambassador Sudradjat, given the limited allocation of funds from the Government of Indonesia for development assistance to friendly countries, the involvement of the private sector was an excellent partnership model, which would greatly assist Indonesia's diplomatic mission in Mozambique.

a5975.speaker: Fachrizal, General Manager of EMP-Buzi Hydrocarbons Pte, Ltd
a5975.name: Fachrizal
a5975.title: General Manager of EMP-Buzi Hydrocarbons Pte, Ltd
a5975.speech: Said that the donation of school desks for elementary schools in Mozambique was a way for the company to express its commitment to improving the quality of education in Mozambique ; added that, although Buzi Hydrocarbon operations in Mozambique had not yet reached the production stage, corporate social responsibility actions were nevertheless being carried out in communities located in the area where the company is located ; according to him, many schools in Mozambique, especially in the province where Buzi Hydrocarbons operates, still do not have sufficient school desks.

a5975.speaker: Lourenco Bulha, Governor of Sofala
a5975.name: Lourenco Bulha
a5975.title: Governor of Sofala
a5975.speech: Welcomed the donation of the 450 desks and has assisted by providing a truck to collect the desks and distribute them among the schools ; said that the desks delivered would benefit more than 3,700 children in Buzi district, and contribute to creating decent learning conditions, allowing more children to enter school and complete their respective levels of education, as well as improving the quality of education overall.

a6110.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.name: Muhammad Pate
a6110.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.speech: Stated that Nigeria anticipated a decline in global financial aid and is actively working towards bolstering its health system by leveraging domestic resources; highlighted that the decline was expected even before the United States government publicly announced cuts to funding for agencies supporting developing countries; reaffirmed Nigeria's commitment to prioritising health, noting the country had made significant advancements in the healthcare sector, and emphasised the government's determination to improve the well-being of citizens, and that the cuts in aid were understandable given the US government's current interests: "Here in Nigeria, we are focused on rebuilding our health system, strengthening domestic resources, and providing services for our citizens" ; "We aim to cooperate with other countries in Africa and globally to enhance biosecurity and health security while fostering private-sector investments."

a6110.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.name: Muhammad Pate
a6110.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.speech: Expressed heartfelt gratitude to the US government for its extensive and generous support over the years, acknowledging the positive impact on Nigeria's healthcare system; said that for the past two decades many countries worldwide have benefited from lifesaving interventions, particularly in HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria, due to the generosity of the US government and its people: "For Nigeria, we sincerely appreciate all the support received" ; "However, it is unwise for any country to rely entirely on another for the health and lives of its population."

a6110.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.name: Muhammad Pate
a6110.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.speech: Revealed that Nigeria had approved the ratification of the African Medicines Agency Treaty, which would help Nigeria become part of a larger African market for locally produced medicines.

a6110.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.name: Muhammad Pate
a6110.title: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6110.speech: Pointed out that there were investment opportunities in Nigeria's health sector, inviting American partners to participate: "We have innovations, tools, systems, and technologies that we can trade. We are open and confident that, as the direction of the US government evolves, Nigeria will continue to welcome genuine partnerships with the US and other countries" ; "These partnerships should be focused on advancing humanity while respecting each nation's interests."

a6110.speaker: Statement issued by Tashikalmah Hallah, Special Adviser on Media and External Relations to the Minister of Health
a6110.name: Statement issued by Tashikalmah Hallah
a6110.title: Special Adviser on Media and External Relations to the Minister of Health
a6110.speech: Issued the statement on Thursday through which the minister made his remarks known.

a6110.speaker: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a6110.name: News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)
a6110.speech: Reports that on 24 January the US administration announced a pause in billions of dollars of foreign aid, affecting nearly all foreign aid programmes, pending a 90-day review.

a6262.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a6262.name: Cesar Chelala
a6262.title: global health consultant
a6262.speech: Stated that although Africa bears one-quarter of the global burden of disease, it only has 2% of the world's doctors.

a6262.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a6262.name: Cesar Chelala
a6262.title: global health consultant
a6262.speech: Noted that there has been a sharp increase in non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, cancer and heart and lung diseases.

a6262.speaker: World Health Organization
a6262.name: World Health Organization
a6262.speech: Estimates that NCDs will rise in the region by 27% over the next 10 years, resulting in 28 million additional deaths.

a6262.speaker: Dr. Crick Lund, Professor of Psychiatry and Mental Health at the University of Cape Town
a6262.name: Dr. Crick Lund
a6262.title: Professor of Psychiatry and Mental Health at the University of Cape Town
a6262.speech: “By neglecting mental health, it will be difficult to attain many of the Sustainable Development Goals related to poverty, malaria, gender empowerment and education.”

a6262.speaker: Sanjeev Ahluwalia, Advisor, Observer Research Foundation in India
a6262.name: Sanjeev Ahluwalia
a6262.title: Advisor, Observer Research Foundation in India
a6262.speech: Argued that health problems are worsened by the lack of health professionals, due in part to the continuing exodus of doctors and nurses to industrialized nations, and that if health care systems are to be effective, resources must be redirected from curative care in urban settings with high tech equipment to primary and preventive health care.

a6262.speaker: Kar and Cartwright-Smith (study)
a6262.name: Kar and Cartwright-Smith (study)
a6262.speech: According to Kar and Cartwright-Smith, Africa is estimated to have lost in excess of $1 trillion in illicit financial flows, roughly equivalent to all of the official development assistance received by Africa during the same timeframe.

a6262.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a6262.name: Cesar Chelala
a6262.title: global health consultant
a6262.speech: Noted that lack of reliable statistics is a hindrance to improving health systems in Africa, ranging from defective systems for civil registration to poor data on maternal and child health indicators, including immunization rates for the most common diseases.

a6262.speaker: World Bank study
a6262.name: World Bank study
a6262.speech: Showed that half the population of African countries had not been included in a census.

a6262.speaker: Cesar Chelala, global health consultant
a6262.name: Cesar Chelala
a6262.title: global health consultant
a6262.speech: According to Chelala, African countries need a different kind of aid: they need their human resources to be trained in their own countries, more help in preventing major diseases, more education for all age levels and better conditions of trade for their products; African countries do not need more monetary aid given irresponsibly, which ends up in the hands of government officials and members of the countries' elites.

a6262.speaker: Paul Theroux, writer
a6262.name: Paul Theroux
a6262.title: writer
a6262.speech: “There are probably more annoying things than being hectored about African development by a wealthy Irish rock star in a cowboy hat, but I can't think of one at the moment.”

a6330.speaker: John Kirby, spokesman for the White House National Security Council
a6330.name: John Kirby
a6330.title: spokesman for the White House National Security Council
a6330.speech: “A ceasefire at this stage would only benefit Hamas,” he told the press on Tuesday, also warning that the situation would get even worse for civilians. While Washington opposes a full ceasefire, he qualified that sporadic pauses in the fighting to facilitate the delivery of aid to the Gaza Strip should be “considered.” ; “We want to see protection measures for civilians. Pauses in operations are a tool, a tactic, that can achieve that for a temporary period (...) but that is not the same thing as a ceasefire.”

a6330.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a6330.name: Joe Biden
a6330.title: US President
a6330.speech: Said on Tuesday that humanitarian aid was not arriving fast enough in the Gaza Strip; the delivery is “not fast enough.”

a6330.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6330.name: Antonio Guterres
a6330.title: UN Secretary-General
a6330.speech: Called for an “immediate humanitarian ceasefire” between Israel and Hamas: “To ease this immense suffering, to make the distribution of aid safer and easier, and to facilitate the release of the hostages, I repeat my call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire,” while denouncing “clear violations” of humanitarian law in Gaza.

a6330.speaker: Eli Cohen, Israeli Foreign Minister
a6330.name: Eli Cohen
a6330.title: Israeli Foreign Minister
a6330.speech: “Mr Secretary-General, what world are you living in,” he said before cancelling his meeting with Antonio Guterres. ; “How can you conclude a ceasefire agreement with someone who has sworn to kill and destroy your very existence.”

a6330.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry
a6330.name: Hamas Health Ministry
a6330.speech: States that 5,791 people have been killed since 7 October and the start of Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip.

a6533.speaker: Ministry of Defense of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a6533.name: Ministry of Defense of the Federal Government of Somalia (press statement)
a6533.speech: A statement released by the Ministry of Defense welcomed the timely support, specifically highlighting the equipment handed over to the Danab forces: “The Ministry particularly welcomes the support of the equipment that was handed over today to the Danab Commando Forces, which will significantly enhance their operational skills in combating terrorism, and help increase the capacity of the National Army in responding to the country's security challenges.”

a6701.speaker: Beatrice Matanje, Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.name: Beatrice Matanje
a6701.title: Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.speech: Emphasized the need for African nations to look inward and fund their own health priorities ; "The path ahead is not paved with aid but with audacity. Africa has the talent, resolve, and ingenuity to build health systems that serve our people."

a6701.speaker: Beatrice Matanje, Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.name: Beatrice Matanje
a6701.title: Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.speech: Highlighted Malawi's commitment to healthcare, citing the allocation of MK5.1 billion to HIV programming to support commodity co-financing, strengthen laboratory sample transport, and recruit frontline health workers.

a6701.speaker: Beatrice Matanje, Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.name: Beatrice Matanje
a6701.title: Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.speech: Stressed the importance of adaptive leadership grounded in evidence, as outlined in the Africa CDC's New Public Health Order.

a6701.speaker: Beatrice Matanje, Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.name: Beatrice Matanje
a6701.title: Chief Executive Officer of Malawi's National Aids Commission (NAC)
a6701.speech: Drew attention to examples of governments taking charge, such as Nigeria's legislature approving an extra $200 million for vaccines and HIV treatment, and Ghana's presidential directive to cover USAid funding gaps.

a6701.speaker: 2001 Abuja Declaration
a6701.name: 2001 Abuja Declaration
a6701.speech: African countries committed to allocating at least 15 percent of their budgets to health.

a6701.speaker: World Health Organisation
a6701.name: World Health Organisation
a6701.speech: Recommends a minimum of $86 (approximately K150,000) per person annually for basic health services.

a6948.speaker: Elisa Kleven, youngest daughter of the artist Lorraine Schneider
a6948.name: Elisa Kleven
a6948.title: youngest daughter of the artist Lorraine Schneider
a6948.speech: Recalls, in an article published earlier this year, that "She simply wanted to make something that no one could argue with."

a6948.speaker: Save the Children
a6948.name: Save the Children
a6948.speech: Says around 468 million children, one young person in six on the planet, live in areas affected by armed conflict; that verified attacks on children have tripled since 2010; and that last year global conflicts killed three times as many children as in 2022.

a6948.speaker: Volker Turk, UN human rights chief
a6948.name: Volker Turk
a6948.title: UN human rights chief
a6948.speech: "The killing and wounding of civilians has become a daily occurrence" ; "Children are being shot. Hospitals bombed. Heavy artillery targets entire communities," said in June when he announced the 2023 figures.

a6948.speaker: United Nations Security Council
a6948.name: United Nations Security Council
a6948.speech: In 2005 identified and condemned six grave violations committed against children in wartime: killing or maiming; recruitment or use by armed forces and armed groups; attacks on schools or hospitals; rape or other grave acts of sexual violence; abduction; and the denial of humanitarian access to those children.

a6948.speaker: UNICEF, the United Nations children's agency
a6948.name: UNICEF
a6948.title: the United Nations children's agency
a6948.speech: Reports that between 2005 and 2023 more than 347,000 grave violations against young people were recorded in more than 30 conflict zones in Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America.

a6948.speaker: Recent study by Italian researchers
a6948.name: Recent study by Italian researchers
a6948.speech: Underlined that "war inflicts serious violations on children's fundamental rights" and found that the complex trauma of war "constitutes a serious threat to children's emotional and cognitive development, increasing the risk of physical and mental illness, disability, social problems and intergenerational consequences."

a6948.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a6948.name: Joe Biden
a6948.title: US President
a6948.speech: "Let there be no mistake, the United States fully, resolutely, totally supports Israel," said recently.

a6948.speaker: Biden administration
a6948.name: Biden administration
a6948.speech: Has acknowledged the likelihood that Israel used American weapons in the Gaza Strip in violation of international law.

a6948.speaker: UNICEF
a6948.name: UNICEF
a6948.speech: Says the Gaza Strip is the most dangerous place in the world for children, and estimates that more than a million children in Gaza - in fact all the children of the Gaza Strip - need psychosocial and mental health services, up from an estimated 800,000 (about 75%) before the current war.

a6948.speaker: Local authorities in Gaza
a6948.name: Local authorities in Gaza
a6948.speech: Say Israel has killed about 17,000 children in the Gaza Strip since the start of the current Gaza war in October 2023.

a6948.speaker: Al Mezan Center for Human Rights (recent report)
a6948.name: Al Mezan Center for Human Rights (recent report)
a6948.speech: Says Israel is committing a "scholasticide", the deliberate and systematic destruction of the Palestinian education system in Gaza.

a6948.speaker: Study by the University of Cambridge, the Centre for Lebanese Studies and UNRWA
a6948.name: Study by the University of Cambridge
a6948.title: the Centre for Lebanese Studies and UNRWA
a6948.speech: Finds that the conflict in Gaza will set children's education back by years and risks creating a generation of Palestinians traumatized for life.

a6948.speaker: Save the Children staff (Lebanon)
a6948.name: Save the Children staff (Lebanon)
a6948.speech: Say that many of the roughly 140,000 children displaced in Lebanon at the end of September arrived at reception centres showing signs of deep distress.

a6948.speaker: Jennifer Moorehead, Save the Children's director in Lebanon
a6948.name: Jennifer Moorehead
a6948.title: Save the Children's director in Lebanon
a6948.speech: "Children tell us they feel that danger is everywhere and that they are never safe. Every loud noise makes them jump" ; "The lives, rights and futures of many children have already been upended and their capacity to cope with this increasingly severe crisis has eroded."

a6948.speaker: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health
a6948.name: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health
a6948.speech: Reports that more than 890 children have been injured by Israeli strikes over the past year, the vast majority (more than 690) since August 20.

a6948.speaker: The Guardian (report published last month)
a6948.name: The Guardian (report published last month)
a6948.speech: Reported that in the small town of Tawila, in North Darfur State, at least ten children die of hunger every day.

a6948.speaker: Aisha Hussien Yagoub, head of the Tawila local government health authority
a6948.name: Aisha Hussien Yagoub
a6948.title: head of the Tawila local government health authority
a6948.speech: "We believe the exact number of children dying of hunger is far higher" ; "Many displaced people from El Fasher live far from our clinic and are unable to get there," told the Guardian.

a6948.speaker: Save the Children
a6948.name: Save the Children
a6948.speech: Says that more than 10 million Sudanese children, 50% of the country's children, found themselves within five kilometres of the conflict's front lines at some point over the past year, the highest exposure rate in the world.

a6948.speaker: Syrian Network for Human Rights
a6948.name: Syrian Network for Human Rights
a6948.speech: Reports that more than 30,200 children have been killed since the start of the Syrian civil war in 2011 and that another 5,200 children have been forcibly disappeared or are under arrest.

a6948.speaker: Rasha Muhrez, director of Save the Children's response in Syria
a6948.name: Rasha Muhrez
a6948.title: director of Save the Children's response in Syria
a6948.speech: "Services had already collapsed after 14 years of conflict" ; "The humanitarian crisis in Syria is reaching a record level. More than two thirds of the Syrian population, including some 7.5 million children, need humanitarian aid," said last month.

a6948.speaker: UNICEF
a6948.name: UNICEF
a6948.speech: Reports that nearly half of Syria's 5.5 million school-age children (2.4 million aged 5 to 17) are still not attending school.

a6948.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a6948.name: Human Rights Watch
a6948.speech: Recently sounded the alarm over the recruitment of children, "apparently with a view to possible transfer to armed groups", by a youth organization affiliated with the Kurdish-led Autonomous Administration for North and East Syria and with the Kurdish-led, US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces.

a6948.speaker: Save the Children
a6948.name: Save the Children
a6948.speech: Says the number of child casualties in Ukraine rose by nearly 40% in the first half of this year, bringing to around 2,200 the total number of children killed or wounded in nearly 900 days of war.

a6948.speaker: Stephane Moissaing, deputy country director of Save the Children in Ukraine
a6948.name: Stephane Moissaing
a6948.title: deputy country director of Save the Children in Ukraine
a6948.speech: "This year the violence has intensified with a new intensity, with missiles, drones and bombs causing an alarming increase in the number of children wounded or killed in explosions in broad daylight" ; "The suffering of families will not stop as long as explosive weapons are used in the populated towns and villages of Ukraine."

a6948.speaker: Munir Mammadzade, UNICEF representative in Ukraine
a6948.name: Munir Mammadzade
a6948.title: UNICEF representative in Ukraine
a6948.speech: "The lack of electricity and all its repercussions this winter could have a devastating impact not only on children's physical health, but also on their mental well-being and their education" ; "Children's lives are taken up with thoughts of survival, not of childhood."

a6948.speaker: Government of Ukraine
a6948.name: Government of Ukraine
a6948.speech: Estimates that Russian authorities have forcibly removed nearly 20,000 children from the occupied territories since the February 2022 invasion.

a6948.speaker: Financial Times investigation
a6948.name: Financial Times investigation
a6948.speech: Revealed that Ukrainian children abducted and taken to Russia early in the war were offered for adoption on a website linked to the Russian government, one under a false Russian identity and another under a Russian version of his Ukrainian name, with the children's Ukrainian origin not mentioned.

a6948.speaker: World Vision
a6948.name: World Vision
a6948.speech: Has described the long-running violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as "one of the worst child protection crises in the world."

a6948.speaker: United Nations report on children and armed conflict (2023)
a6948.name: United Nations report on children and armed conflict (2023)
a6948.speech: Recorded 3,377 grave violations committed against children in the DRC, of which 46% involved the recruitment of children, some as young as five, by armed groups.

a6948.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a6948.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a6948.speech: Reported in May that more than 5,700 schools had been closed in Burkina Faso because of insecurity, depriving more than 800,000 children of their education.

a6948.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council
a6948.name: Norwegian Refugee Council
a6948.speech: Says that by mid-2024 conflicts had led to the closure of more than 14,300 schools in 24 African countries, an increase of 1,100 closures compared with 2023, concentrated in West and Central Africa - mainly Burkina Faso, the DRC, Cameroon, Chad, Nigeria and Niger - and affecting around 2.8 million children.

a6948.speaker: Hassane Hamadou, regional director of the Norwegian Refugee Council for West and Central Africa
a6948.name: Hassane Hamadou
a6948.title: regional director of the Norwegian Refugee Council for West and Central Africa
a6948.speech: "Education is under siege in West and Central Africa. The deliberate targeting of schools and the systemic denial of education because of conflicts is nothing less than a catastrophe. Every day that a child is out of school is a day stolen from their future and from that of their community" ; "We urgently call on all parties to the conflict to cease attacks on and occupation of schools and to ensure that education is protected and treated as a priority."

a6948.speaker: Israa Al-Qahwaji, mental health and psychosocial support coordinator for Save the Children in Gaza
a6948.name: Israa Al-Qahwaji
a6948.title: mental health and psychosocial support coordinator for Save the Children in Gaza
a6948.speech: Told the story of a young boy who survived an air strike that led to the amputation of one of his hands while killing his father and destroying his home; said that in shock and withdrawn the boy was unable to talk about his trauma, but that various therapeutic techniques allowed him to begin to open up, talking about the games he could no longer play and how the loss of his hand had changed his relationships with his friends.

a6948.speaker: Young boy in Gaza, air-strike survivor treated by Save the Children
a6948.name: Young boy in Gaza
a6948.title: air-strike survivor treated by Save the Children
a6948.speech: "Now, are you going to bring my father and give me back my hand?"

a6980.speaker: US administration (announcement)
a6980.name: US administration (announcement)
a6980.speech: Announced on 20 August a new set of sanctions against four magistrates of the International Criminal Court (ICC), for abuse of power in several American and Israeli cases - the Canadian judge Kimberly Prost, the French judge Nicolas Guillou, and two deputy prosecutors, the Fijian Nazhat Shameem Khan [...]

a7048.speaker: Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation of Mozambique
a7048.name: Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation of Mozambique
a7048.speech: At the opening of the event, said that firm responses are needed to this type of crime (cybercrime).

a7048.speaker: Francisco Mabzaia, Chairman of the Board of the Maputo Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMME)
a7048.name: Francisco Mabzaia
a7048.title: Chairman of the Board of the Maputo Municipal Mobility and Parking Company (EMME)
a7048.speech: Says that of the roughly twenty million that would be ideal, the municipal company collects only four million from rotating parking, an amount insufficient to transform Maputo into a city of modern and intelligent systems.

a7048.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a7048.name: Pope Leo XIV
a7048.speech: Expresses solidarity with the victims of the earthquakes in Venezuela and appeals for the strengthening of international humanitarian aid to the populations affected by the tragedy.

a7048.speaker: Fishermen of Inhambane Bay
a7048.name: Fishermen of Inhambane Bay
a7048.speech: Acknowledge the increasingly sharp reduction in seafood and point to the growing pressure exerted on coastal and marine ecosystems.

a7048.speaker: Residents of the village of Niarro, Natikiri neighbourhood, Nampula
a7048.name: Residents of the village of Niarro
a7048.title: Natikiri neighbourhood, Nampula
a7048.speech: Report an increase in crocodile attacks that have already claimed dozens of lives, and ask for the construction of a bridge to make it easier for people and goods to cross.

a7048.speaker: Population of Moma District, Nampula Province
a7048.name: Population of Moma District
a7048.title: Nampula Province
a7048.speech: Asks the Government to rehabilitate the road linking Mogovolas District to the main town of that coastal region.

a7048.speaker: Traders in Moma District
a7048.name: Traders in Moma District
a7048.speech: Say it is very complicated to continue commercial activity because the journey of about two hundred kilometres can take more than ten hours.

a7115.speaker: Philippe Talavera, OYO (Ombetja Yehinga Organisation) Director
a7115.name: Philippe Talavera
a7115.title: OYO (Ombetja Yehinga Organisation) Director
a7115.speech: "When the funding from those partners was suspended, it obviously affected us because we are sub-recipients and rely on that money. So it did affect us. And unfortunately, this year, we could only do fewer projects than we normally do. And we could reach many fewer regions than we normally do."

a7115.speaker: Philippe Talavera, OYO (Ombetja Yehinga Organisation) Director
a7115.name: Philippe Talavera
a7115.title: OYO (Ombetja Yehinga Organisation) Director
a7115.speech: "So it's important to develop the creative sector. But you can only develop the creative sector if people sort of know what it means. For a lot of people, art is a hobby. It's not a job. So we have to start educating people that the creative sector can actually be a job. But as with any job, be it being a doctor, being an engineer, or being a lawyer, it requires training, it requires experience, and it requires exposure. So I think it's important that we encourage young people to explore those opportunities."

a7116.speaker: Dr. Eviness Pemphero Nyalugwe, Malawi Government Focal Person for SSC, and Dr. Babagana, FAO Representative in Malawi
a7116.name: Dr. Eviness Pemphero Nyalugwe
a7116.title: Malawi Government Focal Person for SSC, and Dr. Babagana, FAO Representative in Malawi
a7116.speech: Visited and inspected the site and spoke highly of this achievement: "Advancing the citrus pilot observation [initiative] has laid the foundation for the subsequent introduction of mango and apple varieties," they noted.

a7116.speaker: Liang Suiquan, senior agricultural expert from China's Hubei Province
a7116.name: Liang Suiquan
a7116.title: senior agricultural expert from China's Hubei Province
a7116.speech: "[The] Yichang citrus [fruit] has found a new home in Africa," Liang pointed out, his sentiments not only a testament to the transfer of technology but also the source of inspiration for the event.

a7116.speaker: Liang Suiquan, senior agricultural expert from China's Hubei Province
a7116.name: Liang Suiquan
a7116.title: senior agricultural expert from China's Hubei Province
a7116.speech: "Thank you to my friends and family for helping me realise my dream. I love marathons and I love Malawi's citrus orchards even more," ; he hopes running can serve as a bridge that deepens the friendship between Chinese and Malawian technicians, as they work together toward meeting the 'Four Betters' goal which FAO advances ; described it as a "small, yet beautiful, initiative."

a7116.speaker: Dr. Charles Malidadi, SSC Focal Person at the Ministry of Agriculture's research station
a7116.name: Dr. Charles Malidadi
a7116.title: SSC Focal Person at the Ministry of Agriculture's research station
a7116.speech: "This is the first time I've run on the experimental field with Chinese friends who taught us citrus-grafting techniques. Every step feels like stepping to the rhythm of cooperation."

a7302.speaker: Cassell Anthony Kuoh, founder and CEO of FC Fassell
a7302.name: Cassell Anthony Kuoh
a7302.title: founder and CEO of FC Fassell
a7302.speech: Speaking via phone Tuesday, October 1, 2024 with journalists, Kuoh said clearing the bills was his way of ensuring the players are fully treated; he expressed his commitment to ensuring the players receive appropriate care, stating his hope for their full recovery ahead of the upcoming season: "It is my prayer that all the players including Lorpu Forkap get back to full fitness for the new season."

a7302.speaker: Emmett Glassco, Senior Pro President
a7302.name: Emmett Glassco
a7302.title: Senior Pro President
a7302.speech: Extended gratitude to Kuoh for his generous support, highlighting his positive impact on football development nationwide: "We are very grateful to Kuoh for clearing the bills" ; He described the FC Fassell bank roller as a man with a developmental heart for football across the country: "What Mr. Kuoh did, only a man with a good heart can do such for a club he has no link with."

a7302.speaker: Lorpu Forkpah, FC Fassell goalkeeper
a7302.name: Lorpu Forkpah
a7302.title: FC Fassell goalkeeper
a7302.speech: Conveyed her appreciation for his financial backing and expressed her determination to return to the field soon; told journalists that she is indeed grateful for standing with the club financially, and hopes to be back on her feet very soon and strong.

a7314.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.speech: Regarding the summits of the heads of state of UEMOA and of the Niger Basin Authority, to be held in Cotonou on 08 January 2016, instructions were given to the ministers in charge of Foreign Affairs and of Water to take the appropriate measures to ensure their perfect organisation.

a7314.speaker: Minister in charge of Agriculture of Benin
a7314.name: Minister in charge of Agriculture of Benin
a7314.speech: Reported to the Council on the financing of the cotton campaign.

a7314.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.speech: Expressly instructed the interministerial cotton committee and in particular the Minister of State in charge of the Economy to proceed within 72 hours with the payment of the cotton producers.

a7314.speaker: Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Higher Education of Benin
a7314.name: Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Higher Education of Benin
a7314.speech: Presented to the Council the report on the clearing of the balance of scholarships owed to students for the year 2015.

a7314.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.speech: Instructed the Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Higher Education, in liaison with the Minister of State in charge of the Economy and Finance, to clear within a period of 72 hours the balance for the benefit of the students of the University Social Welfare Centres of Parakou and Abomey-Calavi.

a7314.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.name: Council of Ministers of Benin (communique)
a7314.speech: Instructed the Minister of Water to present to the next Council of Ministers the status of the programme of wells to be drilled throughout the national territory; in the immediate term the Minister of State in charge of the Economy and Finance and the UEMOA commission will make the necessary financial means available to the Military Engineering Corps for the drilling of two hundred (200) wells.

a7314.speaker: Minister of Water of Benin
a7314.name: Minister of Water of Benin
a7314.speech: Presented to the Council, which adopted it, the communication relating to the examination of the financing mechanism for the project to strengthen the drinking water supply systems of the towns of Save, Dassa-Zoume and Glazoue from surface water.
